15:1: As for His saying, may His praise be glorified and His names be sanctified, Alif, Lam, Ra, its explanation has already been presented previously. As for His saying, These are the verses of the Book, it means: these verses, the verses of the books that came before the Qur’an, such as the Torah and the Gospel. And a Qur’an, He says: and verses of a Qur’an. Clear, He says: it makes clear to whoever contemplates and ponders it his guidance and direction. As Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said: Abu Naim told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And a clear Qur’an. He said: It was made clear, and God guided him, gave him the right path, and gave him good. Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Naim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid: Alif, Lam, Ra. The opening words with which he begins his speech. These are the verses of the Book. He said: The Torah and the Gospel. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, “Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book,” he said: The books that came before the Qur’an.
15:2: The readers differed in their reading of his saying perhaps. The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the Kufians read it as perhaps with a light ba, and the majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it with a heavy ba. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings and two well-known languages with one meaning. Each of them has been recited by imams of the reciters, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. The Arabists differed about the meaning of ma that comes with rabb. The grammarians of Basra said: Add ma to rabb to speak about the verb after it. If you wish, you can make ma like shay’, so it is as if you said: Rabb shay’, yuwud meaning Rabb is the word that those who disbelieve love. Some grammarians of Kufa denied this, and said: The source does not need a pronoun, and the word wadd has been used in law, perhaps they would like if they were: that they were. He said: And if the ha is omitted in law, then it is not a direct object, and it is the place of the direct object, and the source should not be translated with anything, and he translated it with something, then made it wadd, then returned it to it as a pronoun, so Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ used to say: The Arabs hardly place rab on the future, but they place it on the past of the verb, like their saying: perhaps I did such-and-such, and perhaps your brother came to me. They said: And it came in the Qur’an with the future: perhaps he would like, and this is only permissible because what was in the Qur’an of promise and threat and what is in it, is true, as if it were evident, so the speech about what was not yet from it ran its course in what was, as it was said And if you could but see when the criminals lower their heads before their Lord and His saying And if you could but see when they are terrified, there is no escape as if it is past and it is expected for its truth in meaning, and that there is no one to deny it, and that the speaker does not say if he forbade or ordered and the one ordered disobeyed him, he says: As for By God, there are many who regret it, remembering what I said about it, knowing that he will regret it. And God and His promise are truer than the words of created beings. It is permissible for perhaps to be accompanied by perhaps even if it is in the wording of yaf’al, as it is said: Perhaps a man dies and there is no shroud for him. And if you give the names, the pronoun kan is with them, as Abu Dawud said: Perhaps the most beautiful camel among them is the one with the most beautiful horses among them The interpretation of the statement: Perhaps those who disbelieved in God and denied His Oneness would wish that they had been Muslims in this world. Ali bin Saeed bin Masrouq Al-Kindi narrated to us: Khalid bin Nafi’ Al-Ash’ari narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Burdah, on the authority of Abi Burdah, on the authority of Abi Musa, who said: It has reached us that when the Day of Resurrection comes and the people of Hell are gathered in Hell along with whomever God wills of the people of the Qiblah, the disbelievers will say to those in Hell from the people of the Qiblah: Are you not Muslims? They will say: Yes. They will say: What good has your Islam done you when you have become with us in Hell? They will say: We had sins, so He seized us for them. So God heard what they said, and He commanded that everyone from the people of the Qiblah who was in Hell be brought out. Then the disbelievers in Hell will say: Oh, would that we were Muslims. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur’an. Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims.” Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated: Amr bin Al-Haitham Abu Qatan Al-Qat’i, Ruh Al-Qaysi, and Affan bin Muslim narrated to us, and the wording is from Abu Qatan. They said: Al-Qasim bin Al-Fadl bin Abdullah bin Abi Jarwah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abbas and Anas bin Malik used to interpret this verse, Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. They said: That is the day when God will gather the sinners among the Muslims and the polytheists in the Fire. Affan said: When the sinners among the Muslims and the polytheists are detained, and the polytheists say: What benefit did you avail you from what you used to worship? Abu Qatan added: It has gathered us and you. Abu Qatan and Affan said: Then God will become angry on their behalf due to His great mercy, and Ruh bin Ubadah did not say that. They all said: Then God will bring them out, and that will be when God says, Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Affan told us, he said: Abu Awana told us, he said: Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Affan told us, he said: Abu Awana told us, he said: Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims, he said: He will enter Paradise and be shown mercy until he says at the end of that: Whoever is a Muslim, let him enter Paradise. He said: So that is his statement: Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish that they were Muslims, that is on the Day of Resurrection, when those who disbelieved will wish that they were monotheists. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan bin Salamah bin Kuhail told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zura’a, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding his statement: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims, he said: This is about the people of Hell when they see them coming out of the Fire. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Ibn Abi Farwa Al-Abdi told us that Ibn Abbas and Anas bin Malik used to interpret this verse, Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims, they used to interpret it as the day when God will detain the sinful Muslims with the polytheists in the Fire. He said: Then the polytheists will say to them: What benefit did what you used to worship in this world avail you? He said: Then God will become angry on their behalf out of His abundant mercy, and He will bring them out, and that is when He will say, Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God will continue to admit people into Paradise, to have mercy on them, and to intercede until He says: Whoever is among the Muslims, let him enter Paradise. That is what He says: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawa’i: Hammad told us: I asked Ibrahim about this verse: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. He said: I was told that the polytheists said to those Muslims who entered the Fire: What good did that which you used to worship avail you? He said: So God becomes angry on their behalf and says to the angels and prophets: Intercede. So they intercede and they are taken out of the Fire, to the point that Satan longs to be taken out with them. He said: At that time, those who disbelieved will wish that they were Muslims. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Hammad told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he said regarding the statement of God Almighty: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims, he said: Those of the polytheists in the Fire will say to the Muslims: There is no god but God has not benefited you. He said: So God becomes angry on their behalf and says: Whoever was a Muslim, let him get out of the Fire. He said: At that time, those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims, he said: The people of Hell will say: We were people of polytheism and disbelief, so what is the matter with these monotheists? How has their worship of Him availed them? He said: Then whoever was in it from the Muslims will be taken out of Hell. He said: Then at that time: Those who disbelieved will wish that they were Muslims. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The people of Hell will say to the monotheists: Your faith has not availed you. He said: When they say that, he said: Bring out whoever has in his heart an atom’s weight of deception. At that time, those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Muslim told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hammad, he said: I asked Ibrahim, about the statement of God Almighty: Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims. He said: The disbelievers taunt the people of monotheism: There is no god but God does not avail you, so God becomes angry on their behalf, so He orders the prophets and angels to intercede, so the people of monotheism are expelled, so much so that Iblis stretches himself out, hoping to be expelled. That is what His statement means: Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims. Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Abd al-Salam told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: This is about the people of Hell when they see them coming out of the fire: Those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said: Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: When God finishes judging between His creation, He says: Whoever is a Muslim, let him enter Paradise, and at that time those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan told me, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims, he said: On the Day of Resurrection. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated: Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ narrated to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims, he said: There are two interpretations. They say: When death approaches the disbeliever, he will wish that he were a Muslim. Others say: Rather, God will punish some people from among the people of monotheism in the Fire for their sins, and the polytheists will recognize them and say: What use has the worship of your Lord been, when He has thrown you into the Fire? So He will become angry on their behalf and bring them out, and He will say: Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-A’aliyah, regarding his statement: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims, he said: It was revealed about those who are brought out of the Fire. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish that they had been Muslims, and by God, that will be on the Day of Resurrection. They will wish that they had been Muslims in this world. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God will continue to admit people into Paradise and intercede until He says: Whoever is among the Muslims, let him enter Paradise. That is when He says: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims.
15:3: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, leave these polytheists to eat in this world what they are eating, and enjoy its pleasures and desires therein until their appointed time, and let hope distract them from taking their share of God’s obedience therein, and from preparing for their afterlife what will bring them closer to their Lord. They will know tomorrow when they come to Him, and they have perished because of their disbelief in God and their polytheism when they see God’s punishment, that they were in loss and ruin because of their enjoyment of the pleasures and desires they were enjoying therein.
15:4: God Almighty says, And We did not destroy, O Muhammad, any of the people of a town of the towns whose people We destroyed in the past except that it had a known decree meaning: except that it had a set term and a known period, We did not destroy them until they reached it, and when they reached it We destroyed them at that time, so He says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So too are the people of your town from which you are, which is Mecca, We do not destroy the polytheists of its people except after their decree has reached its term, because it is My decree that I do not destroy the people of a town except after their decree has reached its term.
15:5: God Almighty says: The destruction of a nation has not come before the appointed time for its destruction, nor has its destruction been delayed beyond the appointed time for it. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, regarding his statement: No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay it, he said: We see that when its term comes, it is not delayed an hour nor brought forward. As for what its term has not come, God delays what He wills and brings forward what He wills.
15:6: God Almighty said: And they said, ‘O you to whom the message has been sent down, you are indeed mad.’
15:7: God the Almighty says: And these polytheists from your people said to you, O Muhammad, O you to whom the message has been sent down, which is the Qur’an in which God mentioned the admonitions to His creation: Indeed, you are mad in calling us to follow you and abandon our gods. If you do not bring us the angels, they said: Why don’t you bring us the angels to bear witness for you to the truth of what you say? If you are of the truthful, meaning: If you are truthful in that God the Almighty sent you to us as a messenger and sent down a book to you, then the Lord who did what you say to you, would not be unable to send an angel from His angels with you as an argument for you against us, and a sign for you of your prophethood and the truth of your statement. The Arabs place the word loma in place of loma and place the word lawla in place of loma, such as the saying of Ibn Muqil: If it were not for modesty and religion, I would have blamed you for some of what is in you, since you blamed my nakedness. He wants: If it weren't for shyness. And similar to what we said about the meaning of remembrance, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: The remembrance was revealed to him, he said: the Qur’an.
15:8: The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement: We do not send down the angels. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it as Ma Tanzil Al-Malaikah with the ta' of tanzall and the fatha and the damma of the angels, meaning: the angels do not send down, on the basis that the action is for the angels. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as Ma Tanzil Al-Malaikah with the nun in nazl and the shaddah of the zay and the accusative of the angels, meaning: we do not send them down, and the angels are then accusative because of the occurrence of nazl upon them. Some of the reciters of Kufa recited it as Ma Tanzil Al-Malaikah with the damma of the angels and the ta' in tanzall, on the basis that the agent is not named. Abu Ja`far said: All of these three readings are close in meaning, because when the angels are sent down by God to one of His messengers, they descend to him, and when they descend to him, they descend only by God sending them down to him. So whichever of these three readings that reciter recites, he is correct in that, although I would prefer that his reciter not go beyond one of the two readings that I mentioned from the recitation of the people of Medina, and the other that the majority of the reciters of Kufa follow, because that is the reading known among the general public, and the other, I mean the reading of the one who recites that which is what is sent down with a damma on the ta’ from tanzall and raf’ al-malikah, is an anomaly and few of those who recite it. The interpretation of the statement: We do not send down Our angels except with the truth, meaning with the message to Our messengers, or with punishment for whomever We want to punish. And if We had sent to these polytheists what they ask for, sending them a sign with you, and they disbelieved, they would not have been given respite to delay the punishment, but they would have been hastened by it, just as We did to the nations before them when they asked for signs and disbelieved when the signs came to them, so We hastened the punishment upon them. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement: We do not send down the angels except with the truth, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: We do not send down the angels except with the truth, he said: with the message and the punishment. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.
15:9: God Almighty says: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, which is the Qur’an, and indeed, We will be its guardian. He said: Indeed, We will be its guardian from adding to it falsehood that which is not from it, or subtracting from it that which is from it of its rulings, limits, and obligations. The ha in His statement: to it is from the remembrance of the remembrance. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan told me: Shababah told us: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: And indeed, We will be its guardians, he said: With Us. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur’an and indeed, We will be its guardian, he said in another verse Falsehood cannot come to it and falsehood is Satan from before it or from behind it. So God sent it down and then preserved it, so Satan cannot add falsehood to it or subtract from it truth, God preserved him from that. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And indeed, We will be its guardians, he said: God protected him from Satan adding falsehood to him, or subtracting from him truth. It was said: The ha in His statement: And indeed, We will be its guardians, is from the mention of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning: And indeed, We will be its guardians from those of his enemies who wish him harm.
15:10: God Almighty says: And We had sent before you among the sects of the former peoples.
15:11: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And We have certainly sent, O Muhammad, messengers before you among the ancient nations. He left out mentioning the messengers, contenting himself with the indication of His statement: And We have certainly sent before you, and he meant by the followers of the ancients: the nations of the ancients, the singular of which is shi’a, and it is also said of a man’s friends: his Shi’a. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We had sent before you among the sects of the ancients, meaning: the nations of the ancients. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And We had sent before you among the sects of the former peoples, he said: among the nations. And His statement: And there came not to them a messenger but they used to ridicule him, meaning: And there came not to the sects of the ancients a messenger from God sent to them calling them to His Oneness and submitting to His obedience, but they used to ridicule him. He says: except that they used to ridicule the messenger whom God sent to them out of their insolence and rebellion against their Lord.
15:12: God Almighty says: Thus do We cause it to enter the hearts of the criminals.
15:13: God Almighty says: Just as We caused the hearts of the sects of the ancients to mock the messengers, so We do that in the hearts of the polytheists of your people who were expelled for disbelief in God. They do not believe in it. He says: They do not believe in the message that was sent down to you. The ha in His statement: We cause it to occur is from the mention of mocking the messengers and denying them. As Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Thus do We cause it to enter the hearts of the criminals, he said: denial. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la urged us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Thus do We cause it to enter the hearts of the criminals, they do not believe in it, he said: If they lie, God causes it to enter their hearts so that they do not believe in it. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: Thus do We cause it to enter the hearts of the criminals, he said: polytheism. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Hamid, he said: I read the entire Qur’an to Al-Hasan in the house of Abu Khalifa, and he interpreted it all in the affirmative, so I asked him about his statement, Thus do We cause it to enter the hearts of the criminals, he said: Deeds that they will do that they did not do. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwaid told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Hamid al-Tawil, he said: I read the entire Qur’an to al-Hasan, and he only interpreted it in a positive way. He said: I stopped him at his lineage, he said: polytheism. Ibn al-Mubarak said: I heard Sufyan say about His statement: We make him, he said: We make him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, “Thus do We cause it to enter the hearts of the criminals. They will not believe in it,” he said: They are as God said, He led them astray and prevented them from believing. It is said from this: He caused it to enter, he causes it to enter, and he causes it to enter, he causes it to enter, and from the reason is the saying of Adi ibn Zayd: I was your enemy's enemy, I did not turn back, and they took you on a difficult day. And from the wiring, another said: Even if they lead them in a strait, they will be driven away as stray camels are driven away. And His statement, And the way of the ancients has passed, the Most High says: Your people, in whose hearts you have put denial, will not believe in this Qur’an until they see the painful punishment, taking from them the way of their ancestors from the polytheists before them from the people of ‘Aad and Thamud and their likes from the nations who denied their messengers, so they did not believe in what came to them from God until God’s wrath descended upon them and they perished. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “Thus do We cause it to enter the hearts of the criminals. They will not believe in it, and the precedent of the former peoples has already passed away.” God’s events with the nations who came before you.
15:14: God Almighty says: And if We opened to them a gate from heaven and they continued therein to ascend.
15:15: The people of interpretation differed regarding the two meanings of His statement, And they continued to ascend therein. Some of them said: The meaning of the statement is: And if We opened to these people who say to you, O Muhammad, Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are of the truthful? a door from heaven and the angels continued to ascend therein, and they saw them clearly, “they would say, ‘Our eyes have only been dazzled. Rather, we are a people bewitched.’” Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And if We opened to them a gate from heaven and they continued therein to ascend, meaning: If We opened to them a gate from heaven and the angels continued to ascend therein, the polytheists would say: He has only taken our sight, and has made us look like we are, and he has only bewitched us. So that is their statement: Why do you not bring us the angels, if you should be of the truthful? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they continued to ascend therein. So the angels continued to ascend therein, and the children of Adam saw them clearly. “They said, ‘Our eyes have only been dazzled. Rather, we are a people bewitched.’” Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: “O you to whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad. Why do you not bring us the angels, if you should be of the truthful?” He said: What is between that and his statement: And even if We opened to them a gate from heaven and they continued therein to ascend? He said: He went back to his statement: Why do you not bring us the angels? What is between that. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: So the angels continued to ascend. Then they looked at them and said, Our eyes have only been dazzled. He said: Quraysh said it. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And if We opened to them a gate from heaven and they continued therein to ascend, he said: Ibn Abbas said: If God opened to them a gate from heaven and the angels continued to ascend therein, he said: they would differ therein, coming and going, they would say, ‘Our eyes have only been dazzled.’ It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And if We opened to them a gate from the heaven and they continued therein to ascend, meaning: the angels. He said: If a gate from the heaven were opened to the polytheists, and they looked at the angels ascending between the heaven and the earth, the polytheists would say: We are a people bewitched, bewitching us, but this is not true. Do you not see that they said before this verse: Why do you not bring us the angels, if you should be of the truthful? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Umar, on the authority of Nasr, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding His statement: And if We opened to them a gate from heaven and they continued therein to ascend, he said: If I were to open a gate from heaven through which the angels could ascend between heaven and earth, the polytheists would say, Rather, we are a people bewitched. Do you not see that they said, Why do you not bring us the angels, if you should be of the truthful? Others said: What is meant by that is: the children of Adam. The meaning of the words, according to them, is: Even if We opened a gate from heaven to these polytheists from your people, O Muhammad, and they continued to ascend through it, they would say, ‘Our eyes have only been dazzled.’ Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And if We opened to them a gate from heaven and they continued therein to ascend, Qatada said, Al-Hasan used to say: If this were done to the children of Adam and they continued therein to ascend, that is, to differ, “they would say, ‘Our eyes have only been dazzled. Rather, we are a people affected by magic.’” As for his saying they ascend, its meaning is: they ascend and climb in it. It is said from this: He ascended and climbed. The singular of ma’arij is ma’raj and mi’raj. From this is the saying of Katheer: According to the way a man was brought up by his father before him, there are ascents to the ladder. It was narrated that ‘Arj, ya’raj, with a kasra on the ‘ra’ in the future tense. And his saying, They said, ‘Our eyes have only been dazzled,’ means: These polytheists, whose description God Almighty described, would have said, This is not true, our eyes have only been dazzled. The reciters differed in their recitation of the phrase I became drunk. The people of Medina and Iraq recited I became drunk with a shaddah on the kaf, meaning: I covered and covered. This is what Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ used to say, as was mentioned to me from him. It was mentioned from Mujahid that he used to recite They said, ‘I became drunk.’ Al-Harith told me that: Al-Qasim told us that he heard Al-Kisa’i narrating on the authority of Hamza, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Mujahid that he read it as our eyes were intoxicated lightly. Mujahid went in his reading of it like that to: our eyes were prevented from seeing and looking from the intoxication of the wind, which is its stillness and stagnation. It is said from it: the wind became still and stagnant. It has been narrated on the authority of Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala’ that he used to say: It is taken from the intoxication of drink, and that its meaning is: intoxication has covered our eyes. As for the people of interpretation, they differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: The meaning of sakrat is was blocked. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Our eyes are covered, he said: They are blocked. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Hajjaj told us, meaning Ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Kathir told me: It was blocked. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, in his statement: Our sight was intoxicated, meaning: blocked. So it is as if Mujahid went in his statement, and his interpretation of that is: blocked, to that it means: prevented sight, just as water is intoxicated and prevented from flowing by being confined in a place by the intoxication with which it is intoxicated. Others said: The meaning of sakrat is took. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They said, ‘Our eyes have only been dazzled.’ He said: Our eyes have been taken. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He only took our sight, and made it appear to us, and only made us subject. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, They said, ‘Our eyes have only been dazzled.’ He said: Our eyes have been bewitched. He said: Our eyes have been taken. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said: Shaiban told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Whoever reads sakrat with a shaddah means was blocked. And whoever reads sakrat with a light sakrat, then he means was bewitched. It is as if these people directed the meaning of his saying sakrat to the fact that their eyes were bewitched, so what they saw was confused for them, so they could not distinguish between what was correct in what they saw and what was not, from the saying of the Arabs: Sakrat ‘ala fulan ra’i his opinion became confused for him, if his opinion regarding what he wanted was confused for him, so he did not know what was right in it and what was not. So if he resolved on an opinion, they said: The confusion has gone away from him. Others said: It is taken from sugar, and its meaning is: our eyesight is clouded so we cannot see, as drunkenness does to its owner, so when he is intoxicated and his eyesight is clouded like poison, he cannot see. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement: Our eyes were only dazzled, he said: Dazzled, the drunkard who does not reason. Others said: The meaning of this is: I went blind. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Al-Kalbi: I became blind. He said: I went blind. The most correct of these sayings, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: Our eyes have been taken and bewitched, so they do not see the thing as it is, and the edge of their sight has gone, and its light has been extinguished, just as it is said of a hot thing when its fervor has gone and the edge of its heat has subsided: it has become intoxicated. Al-Muthanna bin Jandal al-Tahawi said: Winter came, the grave was covered with snow, the snake became ugly and appeared Made the hot eye drunk That is, it settles, goes away, and is extinguished. Dhu al-Rummah said: Rather, the crack of dawn, the abandonment, and their wading through the night when he is drunk Meaning: when its turbulence subsides. It was reported on the authority of Qais that she says: The wind became intoxicated, intoxicated, sakuraan, meaning: it became still. Even if that is correct on her authority, the meaning of sakara and sakara with the emphasis and the stress are close, except for the reading that I do not permit other than it in the Qur’an is sakara with the emphasis due to the consensus of the authority of the reciters on it, and it is not permissible to contradict it in what it came with consensus on.
15:16: God Almighty says: And We have certainly made in the lowest heaven mansions for the sun and the moon, and they are planets that the sun and the moon descend upon. And We have adorned them for the observers. He says: And We have adorned the heaven with planets for whoever looks at it and sees it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And We have certainly placed constellations in the heaven, he said: the planets. Bishr told us, he said: Suwaid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We have certainly placed in the heaven constellations, and its constellations are its stars. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Buruj means the planets.
15:17: God Almighty says: And We have protected it from every accursed devil.
15:18: God Almighty says: And We have protected the lowest heaven from every accursed devil whom God has stoned and cursed, except for he who eavesdrops. He says: But some devils may eavesdrop on what is happening in the heaven, and a meteor of fire follows him, clearly showing its effect on him, either by confusing and corrupting him, or by burning him. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say that his statement, except for the one who eavesdrops, is an exception, just as he said, I complain only of good, meaning, but I remember good. Some of them used to deny that when he said it, and say, If except means but I knew, then the function of but is not necessary to imply remember. And he says, If the matter required implying remember, then the statement of the speaker, ‘Zayd stood up, not Amr,’ would require implying mention. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Affan bin Muslim told us: Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The devils ascend in groups, eavesdropping. He said: Then the rebellious one among them rises alone, and a meteor is thrown at him, and it hits his forehead or his side, or wherever God wills of it, and he is engulfed in flames. He comes to his companions while he is engulfed in flames, and he says: Such and such happened. He said: Then those people go to their brothers among the priests, and they add to it many times more lies, and they tell them about it. Then if they see something of what they said, they believe them in the lies they brought them. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And We have preserved it from every accursed devil, except for one who steals a hearing, he said: He meant to steal a hearing, and it is like his statement: Except for one who steals a glance. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Except for he who steals a hearing is similar to his statement: Except for he who snatches a snatch and is pursued by a piercing flame. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, Except for he who steals a hearing, he said: snatches a snatch. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement: Except for one who eavesdrops, it is like His statement: Except for one who snatches a snatch and is pursued by a piercing flame. Ibn Abbas used to say: Meteors do not kill, but they burn, disorient, and injure without killing. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, From every accursed devil. He said: The accursed: the cursed. He said: Al-Qasim said on the authority of Al-Kisa’i: that he said: stoning in the entire Qur’an: is cursing.
15:19: He, the Most High, means by His saying: And the earth We have spread out: And the earth We have spread out and made it smooth. And We have cast therein firm mountains He says: And We have cast firm mountains on its backs, meaning stable mountains. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And the earth We have spread out. And he said in another verse And the earth after that He spread it out. And he mentioned to us that the mother of cities is Mecca, and from it the earth was spread out. His statement, And We cast therein firm mountains, its firm mountains are its mountains. We have explained the meaning of anchoring previously with evidence that suffices us from repeating it. And his statement, And We caused to grow therein of every well-balanced thing, means: And We caused to grow in the earth of every well-balanced thing, meaning: of every well-measured thing, and by a certain limit. Known. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We caused to grow therein of every well-balanced thing, meaning: known. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told us, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We caused to grow therein of every well-balanced thing, meaning: known. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, or on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding his statement, of everything there is a measure, he said: according to a certain amount. Al-Muthanna told us: Amr bin Awn told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih or on the authority of Abu Malik, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hammani told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, of everything there is a measure. He said: according to a certain amount. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Ali told us, meaning Ibn Al-Ja’d, who said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah: For everything there is a measure. He said: According to a certain amount. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: According to a certain amount. Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, From everything there is a measure. He said: It is known. Mujahid bin Musa told us: Yazid told us: Abdullah bin Yunus told us: I heard Al-Hakam bin Utaybah and Abu Makhzum asked him about his saying, of everything is measured. He said: of everything is measured. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Yazid bin Harun told us: Abdullah bin Yunus told us: I heard Al-Hakam, and Abu Urwa asked him about the statement of God Almighty, For everything there is a measure. He said: For everything there is a measure. This is what Al-Hasan said, and Abu Urwa asked him. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, of everything is measured, he said: It is determined by a measure. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, of everything there is a measure. He said: It is determined by a measure. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ali bin Al-Haitham told us, he said: Yahya bin Zakariya told us, on the authority of Ibn Jarj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: It is predestined by destiny. Al-Muthanna told us: Ali bin Al-Haitham told us: Yahya bin Zakariya told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh: Everything is balanced. He said: According to a certain amount. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We caused to grow therein of every well-balanced thing, meaning: known. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, of everything there is a measure, meaning: known. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: And We caused to grow in the mountains every kind of weighted thing: meaning gold, silver, copper, lead, and other things that are weighed. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And We caused to grow therein of every well-balanced thing, he said: The things that are weighed. The first of the two opinions is more correct in our view, due to the consensus of the scholars of interpretation on it.
15:20: God Almighty says: And We have made for you O people on earth ways of livelihood the plural of livelihood and for those for whom you are not providers. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His statement, And for whom you are not providers. Some of them said: He meant by it the beasts and livestock. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us all, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And for whom you are not providers means the animals and the livestock. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Others said: He meant by that: the beast in particular. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, regarding this verse, And for whom you are not providers, he said: The wild beast. So the interpretation of who in and for whom you are not providers, according to this interpretation, means what, and that is rare in the speech of the Arabs. This is more correct and better to say: He meant by his statement and those for whom you are not providers the male and female slaves, beasts of burden and livestock. So the meaning of that is: And We made therein livelihoods, and the male and female slaves, beasts of burden and livestock. If that is the case, it is good to then put min in place of the slaves, the female slaves and the beasts of burden, because the Arabs do that when they want to talk about the animals with them, the sons of Adam. This interpretation, according to what we have said and to which we have diverted the meaning of the speech, if min is in the accusative case, in apposition to livelihoods, meaning: We made therein livelihoods for you, and We made therein those for whom you are not providers. It was said: Min is in the position of a genitive case, in apposition to the kaf and the mim, in his saying And We made for you meaning: And We made for you therein livelihoods and for whom you are not providers. I think that Mansur in his saying he is the beast intended this meaning and he meant it, and even if it has a face in the speech of the Arabs, it is a little far-fetched, because it is hardly consistent with a meaning in the case of genitive case, and perhaps it came in the poetry of some of them in the case of necessity, as some of them said: I did not ask about them, by Dhu al-Jamajim, and Abu Naim, the one with the torn banner. Abu Naim responded to the ha and mim in about them. I have shown the ugliness of that in their speech.
15:21: God Almighty says: There is no rain but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except in due measure for every land, the limit and amount of which are known to Us. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Idris told us: Yazid bin Abi Ziyad told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: There is no land that has more rain than another land, but God decrees it on earth. Then he recited: “And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories. And We do not send it down except according to a known measure.” Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Juhaifa, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: No year is rainier than another year, but God diverts it from whomever He wills. Then he said: “And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories. And We do not send it down except according to a known measure.” Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Ibrahim bin Mahdi Al-Masisi told us: Ali bin Mashair told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Juhaifa, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud: No year has more rain than another year, but God distributes it as He wills, a year here and a year there. Then he recited: “And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories. And We do not send it down except according to a known measure.” Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: And there is nothing but that with Us are its depositories. He said: Rain in particular. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Ismail bin Salim told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, regarding His statement: And We do not send it down except according to a known measure, he said: No year has more rain than another year, nor less, but some people are given rain and others are deprived, and it may be in the sea. He said: And it has reached us that with the rain there descend from the angels more than the number of the children of Iblis and the children of Adam, counting every drop wherever it falls and what it produces.
15:22: The reciters differed in their recitation of this, so most reciters read it as And We sent the fertilizing winds, and some reciters from Kufa read it as And We sent the fertilizing wind, so they made the wind singular, and it is described by the plural, I mean by his saying: fertilizing. The meaning of this should be: that the wind, even if its wording is one, its meaning is plural, because it is said: the wind came from every direction, and blew from every place, so it was said: fertilizing for that reason, so the meaning of their plural is its description, and it is one in wording, the meaning of their saying: a fine dust, a land of fools, and a garment of morals, as the poet said: Winter has come and my shirt is a bunch of morals that the yearning one laughs at The Arabs do the same with everything that is spacious. The Arabists differed about the reason for describing the winds as pollinating. It is actually pollinating, not fertilizing, because it pollinates the clouds and trees. It is only described as pollinating, not fertilizing, as one says: a fertilizing camel. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It was said: The winds are fertilizing, so he made it on the fertilizing, as if the winds were pollinating, because there is good in them, so they were pollinated with good. He said: Some of them said: The winds pollinate the clouds, so this indicates that meaning, because if they create it and there is good in it, that reaches it. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: There are two meanings in that: One of them is to make the wind the one that pollinates by passing over the dirt and water, so the pollen is in it, so it is said: a fertilizing wind, as one says: a fertilizing camel. He said: And evidence for that is that he described the wind of torment, so he said: upon them is the barren wind, so he made it barren if it did not pollinate. He said: The other aspect is that it is described as being fertilized, even though it is fertilized, as it was said: a sleeping night and sleep in it, and a secret that is kept, and as it was said: the prominent and the sealed, so he made it prominent, and did not say prominent, and he built it on something other than his action: meaning that that is one of his attributes, so the passive participle is permissible for the passive participle, just as the active participle is permissible for the passive participle, if the construction is not intended on the action, as it was said: gushing water. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that the winds are fertilisers, as described by the Most High, the Most Praised, in their description. Even if they fertilise the clouds and trees, they are fertilisers and pollinators. The water carries them, and the fertilisation of the clouds and trees is its work in them. This is as Abdullah ibn Masoud said. Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Qais bin Sakn, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, regarding his statement, And We send the winds as inseminators, he said: God sends the winds, and they carry water, and the clouds flow, and they produce as a she-camel produces, and then it rains. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Qais bin Sakn, on the authority of Abdullah: And We send the winds as fertilisers. He said: God sends the wind, which fertilises the clouds, then it makes them flow and they produce fruit as a she-camel produces fruit, then it rains. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Asbat bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Qais bin Al-Sakn, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, regarding his statement, And We send the winds as fertilizing agents, he said: He sends the winds, and they carry water from the clouds, then they pass over the clouds, and they produce milk as a she-camel produces milk. Abdullah explained with his statement, He sends the winds, and they carry water, that they are the fertilizing agents by carrying it, even though they are fertilized by their pollination of the clouds and trees. As for another group of people of interpretation, they attributed God Almighty’s description of it as fertile to it meaning fertilized, and that fertilized was placed in the place of fertilized, as Nahshal bin Hari said: Let Yazid weep, the miserable one, in supplication, and the disheveled one, who has been tossed aside by calamities. He wants the mills, as Al-Nabigha said: I am tired of them, O Umaima, and I am suffering a night in which the stars are slow Meaning: position. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: And We sent the winds as fertilisers, he said: They fertilise the clouds. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Naim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And We sent the winds as fertilisers, he said: They fertilise the trees. I said: Or the clouds? He said: And the clouds are pollinated until it rains. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Ishaq bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair, he said: God sends the bringer of good tidings, and the earth is shaken. Then God sends the stirrer, and she stirs the clouds. Then God sends the reconciler, and she reconciles the clouds. Then God sends the pollinators, and they pollinate the trees. Then Ubayd recited: And We sent the pollinating winds. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And We sent the winds as fertilisers, meaning: fertilisers for the clouds, and some of the winds are torment, and some of them are mercy. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Lawaqih means: the water scatters in the clouds. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: fertilizers he said: they pollinate the trees and cause the clouds to pass through. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Concerning His statement, And We sent the winds as fertilisers, the winds are sent by God upon the clouds, so they fertilise them, and they become filled with water. Abu Kuraib told us: Ahmad bin Yunus told us: Isa bin Maimun told us: Abu Al-Muhazzam told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The south wind is from Paradise, and it is the fertilizing wind, and it is the one that God Almighty mentioned in His Book, and in it are benefits for people. Abu al-Jamahir al-Himsi or al-Hadrami Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman told me: Abd al-Aziz ibn Musa told us: Isa ibn Maimun Abu Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Mahzoom, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar. And His statement, Then We sent down water from the sky and gave it to you to drink, the Most High says: Then We sent down rain from the sky and gave you to drink that rain for your land and your livestock to drink. If its meaning was: We sent it down for you to drink, it would have been said: Then We gave you to drink it. This is because the Arabs say when they give a man water to drink or milk or something else: I gave him water without an alif if it was for his to drink. And if they make water for him for his land or livestock to drink, they say: I gave him water and I gave him to drink. And likewise if you ask for water for him, they say: I gave him water and I asked him to drink, as Dhu al-Rummah said: I stopped at a drawing of my camel, Lamia, and I still cry and talk to it I watered it until its stones and playgrounds almost spoke to me. Likewise, if you give a man a hide to make a water skin, you say: I gave him a drink from it. And His statement, And you are not its keepers, means: And you are not its keepers of the water that We sent down from the sky and gave you to drink, so you prevent it from being given to me, because that is in My hand and to Me, I give it to whomever I wish, and I prevent it from whomever I wish.
15:23: God Almighty says: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the inheritors.
15:24: God Almighty says: And We have certainly known those among you who went ahead, and We have certainly known those who came after.
15:25: God the Almighty says: And indeed, it is We who give life to whoever was dead if We will, and cause death to whoever was alive if We will, and We are the inheritors meaning: We inherit the earth and whoever is on it by causing them all to die, so that no living being will remain except Us when that appointed time comes. And His statement: And We have certainly known those of you who went before, and We have certainly known those of you who came after. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: We have certainly known those of the nations who have passed, and their destruction has already occurred, and those who were created while they were alive, and those who have not yet been created from among those who will be created. Who said that? Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, And We have certainly known those among you who went before, and We have certainly known those who came after. He said: Those who went before are those of the nations who were created and those who passed away, and those who came after are those who were not created. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam told us: Amr ibn Qays told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Masruq, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, And We have certainly known those among you who went before, and We have certainly known those who came after, he said: They are all of God’s creation. He has known those of them whom He created until today, and He has known who will create them after today. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn al-Tamimi told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: God created creation and finished with them. The forerunners are those who emerged from creation, and the latter are those who remained in the loins of men and did not emerge. Muhammad ibn Abi Ma'shar told me: Abu Ma'shar told me: I heard Awn ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud discussing with Muhammad ibn Ka'b the words of God, And We have certainly known those among you who went forward, and We have certainly known those who lag behind. Awn ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud said: The best rows of men are the front ones, and the worst rows of men are the back ones, and the best rows of women are the back ones, and the worst rows of women are the front ones. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It is not like that. We have certainly known those among you who went forward: the dead and the killed. And those who lag behind: those who will join them after them, and it is your Lord who will gather them. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing. Awn ibn Abdullah said: May God guide you and reward you with good. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, who said: Qatada said: The forerunners are those who have passed away, and the latter are those who remain in the loins of men. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Saeed bin Mansour told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us: Saeed bin Masruq told us, on the authority of Ikrimah and Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And We certainly knew those among you who went ahead, and We certainly knew those who remained behind, they said: those who died and those who remained. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We have certainly known those among you who went before, he said: Ibn Abbas used to say: Adam, peace be upon him, and those of his descendants who passed on. And We have certainly known those who came after, he said: those who remained in the loins of men. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And We have certainly known those among you who went before, and We have certainly known those who came after. He said: The ones who went before were Adam and those after him, until this verse was revealed. And the later ones: He said: Everyone who was from his descendants. Abu Jaafar said: I think he said: What was not created, and what is created. Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: The forerunners are those who came out of the loins of men. And the later ones are those who have not yet come out. Then he recited: “And indeed, your Lord will gather them. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.” Others said: He meant by the earlier ones: those who had perished, and the later ones: the living who had not perished. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told us: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We have certainly known those among you who went before, and We have certainly known those who came after. He means by those who went before: those who died, and he means by those who came after: those who are alive and have not died. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And We have certainly known those among you who went before, meaning: the dead among you, And We have certainly known those who came after, the remainder of them, who are the living, saying: We have known who died and who remained. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And We certainly knew those among you who went before, and We certainly knew those who came after, he said: Those among you who went before are those who passed away among the first nations. And those who came after are those who remain. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: We knew those who came before at the beginning of creation, and those who came after at the end of them. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abdul Wahhab told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, regarding this verse, And We have certainly known those among you who went before, and We have certainly known those who came after. He said: He said: The first of creation and the last of it. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement, And We have certainly known those among you who went forward, and We have certainly known those who came after, what was advanced at the beginning of creation, and what was delayed at the end of creation. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Ali bin Asim told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Amer, regarding his statement: And We have certainly known those of you who went before, he said: In the afternoon, and those of you who came after in the loins of men and the wombs of women. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: We have known the earlier nations and the later ones of the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us all, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Those who have come before you means the first generations, and those who come after: the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us: Abdul Malik told me, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And We have certainly known those among you who went before, and We have certainly known those who came after. He said: Those who went before: the nations that have passed, and those who came after: the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar, but he did not mention Qais. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: We know those of you who have gone before in goodness, and those who have come after it. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We have certainly known those among you who went ahead, and We have certainly known those who came after. He said: Al-Hasan used to say: Those who went ahead were in obedience to God, and those who came after were in disobedience to God. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Rashid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Those who are ahead in goodness, and those who are behind: he says: those who are slow to do it. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: We know those of you who are ahead in the rows in prayer, and those who are behind in it, because of the women. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man who told us, on the authority of Marwan bin Al-Hakam, that he said: There were people who used to stay behind in the rows because of the women. He said: Then God revealed: And We have certainly known those among you who go forward, and We have certainly known those who lag behind. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ja`far bin Sulayman told us: Amr bin Malik told me: I heard Abu al-Juza’ say about the words of God, And We have certainly known those among you who go forward, and We have certainly known those who lag behind. He said: Those among you who go forward in the rows in prayer and those who lag behind. Muhammad bin Musa Al-Harsi told me: Nuh bin Qais told us: Amr bin Malik told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A woman used to pray behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas said: No, by God, I have never seen anyone like her. When some of the Muslims prayed, they would go forward and some would go back. When they prostrated, they would look at her from beneath their hands. Then God revealed: And We have certainly known those among you who go forward and those who lag behind. Abu Kurayb narrated: Ubayd God Musa narrated: Nuh ibn Qays informed us, and Abu Kurayb narrated: Malik ibn Ismail informed us, on the authority of Nuh ibn Qays, on the authority of Amr ibn Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There was a beautiful woman who was one of the most beautiful people who used to pray behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of the people would move forward in the first row so that he would not see her, and some of them would move back until they were in the last row. When he bowed, he would look from under his armpits in the row. So God revealed concerning her, And We have certainly known those among you who go forward, and We have certainly known those who lag behind. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the statements in my opinion regarding this is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of this is: And We have certainly known those among you who are dead, O children of Adam, whose death has come before, and We have certainly known those who will come after, those whose death has come after, from among those who are alive and from those who have not yet come after, based on the indication of what preceded it from the speech, which is His saying: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the inheritors, and what follows it, which is His saying: And indeed, it is your Lord who will gather them, on the basis that this is so, since it was between these two reports, and there was no speech before that that indicated otherwise, nor did it come after, and it is possible that it was revealed regarding those who are ahead in the row, regarding the women and those who are behind in it for that reason, then God Almighty would have included in the intended meaning all of creation, so He, the Most High, said to them: We have certainly known what has passed of creation and We have counted them, and what they used to do, and who is alive among you, and who will come after you, O people, and the deeds of all of you, their good and their evil, and We have counted all of that, and We will gather all of them, so We will reward each one according to his deeds, if good. So good, and if evil, then evil, then this is a threat and warning to those who are behind in the rows for the sake of women, and to everyone who transgresses the limits of God, and does what He has not permitted him to do, and a promise to those who advance in the rows for the sake of women, and hasten to the love and pleasure of God in all his actions. And His saying: And indeed, your Lord will gather them together, meaning by that, may His praise be glorified: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, will gather all of the first and the last before Him on the Day of Resurrection, the people of obedience among them and the disobedient, and everyone of His creation, those of them who came before and those who came after. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And your Lord will gather them together. He said: meaning the first and the last. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Abu Khalid Al-Qurashi told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And indeed, your Lord will gather them together, he said: This is from here, and this is from there. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And your Lord will gather them together, he said: And all of them will die, then their Lord will gather them together. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Ali bin Asim told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Amer: And your Lord will gather them together, he said: God will gather them all together on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan said: Ali said: Dawud said: I heard Amer interpreting his statement: He is Wise, Knowing, saying: Your Lord is Wise in His management of His creation, in giving them life when He gives them life, and in causing them to die when He causes them to die. He is Knowing of their number and their deeds, and of those among them who are alive and those who are dead, and of those who have gone before and those who will stay behind. As Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said: God has known all of them, meaning the predecessors and the successors.
15:26: God Almighty says: And We created Adam, who is man, from clay. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of clay. Some of them said: It is dry clay that has not been touched by fire, so if you tap it, it clinks, and you hear it clink. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya bin Saeed and Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Adam was created from clay, from mud and from sticky clay. As for sticky, it is good. As for mud, it is sludge. As for clay, it is fine dust. He was only called a human being because he was entrusted with something and he forgot. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We created man from clay, he said: And clay is the dry soil from which a clanging is heard. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: From clay, from black mud, he said: Clay is dry mud from which a squeaking sound is heard. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Hameed bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Saleh, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: From clay. He said: Clay is water that falls on good earth, then it is removed from it, so it cracks, then it becomes like thin pottery.
