Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Man was created from three things: sticky clay, clay, and aged black mud. Sticky clay is the good adhesive, clay is the thin clay from which pottery is made, and aged black mud is the clay in which there is mud. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We created man from clay from altered black mud, he said: It is dry soil that becomes wet after it dries. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Clay is that which clatters, like pottery made of good clay. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: As-Salsal is hard clay mixed with sand dunes. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, from clay, he said: dry soil. Others said: Salsal means stinking. It is as if they attributed that to the fact that it is from their saying: Salt the meat and Asl: If you are, and that is said in both languages: Yaf’al and Af’al. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, From clay. Clay means stinking. What is more appropriate for the verse is that the clay in this place has a sound of clanging, and that is because God Almighty described it in another place when He said He created man from clay like pottery, so He, the Most High, likened it to being like pottery in its dryness. If its meaning was that it was stinking, He would not have likened it to pottery, because pottery is not stinking, so that it would be likened to something else in its stinking. As for his saying, from black mud, black mud is the plural of ham’ah, which is mud that has turned black. His saying, black mud, means: changed. Scholars of Arabic speech differed about the meaning of his statement masnun. Some of the Basran grammarians said: He meant by it: perfect, shaped mud. It was mentioned about the Arabs that they said: sun on the model of sunnat al-wajh: meaning its image. He said: And as if the sunnat of something is from that: meaning its example that it was placed on. He said: And it is not from the changed, stagnant, because it is from sunnan muddaa’ib. Another of them said: It is poured mud. He said: And poured is the well-watered, and it is from their saying: I poured water on the face and other things if I poured it. Some of the people of Kufa used to say: It is the variable. He said: It is as if it was taken from the sharpening of a stone on a stone, which is when one of them rubs against the other. It is said: I sharpened it, I sharpened it, so it is sharpened. He said: And what comes out from between them is called: Sinin, and that is foul-smelling. He said: It was named Al-Musnun from it because iron is sharpened on it. As for the people of interpretation, they said something similar to what we said about it. Who said that? Ubaidullah bin Yusuf al-Jubayri told us: Muhammad bin Katheer told us: Muslim told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: from black mud, he said: The mud is the stinking one. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: From black mud. He said: That which has become putrid. Abu Kuraib told us: Uthman bin Saeed told us: Bishr bin Amara told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: From black mud. He said: stinking. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, from black mud, he said: It is wet, stinking dirt, then it was made into clay like pottery. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: Shibl told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: From black mud, he said: stinking. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: From aged black mud. Aged black mud is that which has changed and become putrid. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar: From old black mud. He said: It has become foul. He said: It is foul-smelling. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement, from black mud, he said: from sticky clay, which is the sticky part of the sand dune. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: from black mud, he said: stinking mud. Others said: It is wet clay. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, from black mud, meaning: from moist clay.
15:27: God Almighty says: And the jinn. We have previously explained the meaning of the jinn, and why it is called jinn. What is meant by the jinn here is Iblis, the father of the jinn. God Almighty says: And Iblis, We created before man from scorching fire. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the jinn We created before, and he is Iblis, who was created before Adam, and Adam was created last of creation, so the enemy of God, Iblis, envied him for the honor that God had given him, so he said: I am fire, and this is clay, so the prostration was for Adam, and the obedience was for God, the Most High, mentioned, so He said Then get out of it, for you are expelled. The interpreters differed about the meaning of poisonous fire. Some of them said: It is the hot poison that kills. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And the jinn - We created them before from scorching fire, he said: The hot scorching fire that kills. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hammani told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the jinn - We created them before from scorching fire. He said: They are the scorching fires that kill, then a hurricane in which there was fire struck them and they were burned. He said: They are the scorching fires that kill. Others said: He means by that from the flames of fire. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: And the jinn - We created them before from scorching fire, he said: from a flame of scorching fire. Abu Kuraib told us: Uthman told us, on the authority of Saeed, who said: Bishr bin Ammarah told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Iblis was from a tribe of angels called the jinn, who were created from the scorching fire from among the angels. He said: And the jinn who were mentioned in the Qur’an were created from a smokeless flame of fire. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Abu Dawud narrated: Shu`bah narrated: Abu Ishaq narrated: I went to visit `Amr ibn al-Asam, and he said: Shall I not tell you a hadith that I heard from `Abdullah? I heard `Abdullah say: These poisons are one of seventy parts of the poisons from which the jinn emerged. He said: Then he recited: And the jinn - We created them before from scorching fire. Some of the Arab scholars used to say: The poisons are by night and by day. Some of them said: The heat is by day, and the poisons are by night. It is said: The poison of our day is poisonous. Al-Muthanna told me: Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar told us: Ismail ibn Abd al-Karim told us: Abd al-Samad ibn Maqal told me: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih being asked about the jinn, what they are, and do they eat, drink, die, or intermarry? He said: They are of different kinds. As for the pure jinn, they are a kind of wind that does not eat, drink, die, or reproduce. And among them are kinds that eat, drink, intermarry, and die, and these are the ones that include the ghoul, the ghoul, and the like.
15:28: God Almighty said: And when your Lord said to the angels, ‘Indeed, I am creating a human being from clay from altered black mud.’
15:29: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And remember, O Muhammad, when your Lord said to the angels, ‘Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay from altered black mud. * Then when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit,’ so he became a living human being, ‘then fall down to him in prostration.’” A prostration of greeting and honor, not a prostration of worship. Ja'far ibn Mukram told me: Abu Asim told us: Shabib ibn Bishr told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When God created the angels, He said: I am creating a human being from clay, so when I create him, prostrate to him. They said: We will not do that. So He sent fire upon them and burned them. Then He created other angels and said: I am creating a human being from clay, so when I create him, prostrate to him. But they refused. So He sent fire upon them and burned them. Then He created other angels and said: I am creating a human being from clay, so when I create him, prostrate to him. But they refused. So He sent fire upon them and burned them. Then He created angels and said: I am creating a human being from clay, so when I create him, prostrate to him. They said: We hear and obey, except for Iblis, who was among the first disbelievers.
15:30: God Almighty said: Then the angels prostrated themselves all together.
15:31: God Almighty said: Except Satan, he refused to be with those who prostrated.
15:32: God Almighty says: When God created that human being and breathed the spirit into him after He had formed him, all the angels prostrated together, except for Iblis, for he refused to be with those who prostrated to Adam when they prostrated, so he did not prostrate to him with them out of arrogance, envy and malice. So God Almighty said: He said, ‘O Iblis, what is the matter with you that you are not with those who prostrate?’ He says: What prevented you from being with those who prostrated? According to some of the Kufi grammarians, it is a genitive, and according to some of the people of Basra, it is an accusative because of the absence of the preposition.
15:33: God Almighty said: He said, ‘I would never prostrate to a human being whom You created from clay from altered black mud.’
15:34: God Almighty said: He said, 'Then get out of it, for you are expelled.'
15:35: God Almighty says, He said, Iblis, I would not prostrate to a human being whom You created from clay from altered black mud, and he is from clay and I am from fire, and fire eats clay. And His saying, Then get out of it, God Almighty says, Iblis, Then get out of it, for you are expelled. And the cursed is the cursed, it was changed from maf’ul to fa’il, which is the cursed one, and this is what a group of people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then you are accursed, and the accursed is the cursed. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: Then get out of it, for indeed, you are expelled, he said: cursed. Stoning in the Qur’an means cursing. And His statement: And upon you is the curse until the Day of Judgment, meaning: And if God becomes angry with you by expelling you from the heavens and banishing you from them until the Day of Recompense, which is the Day of Resurrection. We have explained the meaning of the curse in more than one place, so there is no need to repeat it here.
15:36: God Almighty said: He said, ‘My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day they are resurrected.’
15:37: God Almighty said: He said, 'Then you are among those granted respite.'
15:38: God Almighty says: Iblis said: My Lord, since You have brought me out of the heavens and cursed me, then delay me until the day when You will resurrect Your creation from their graves and gather them for the Day of Resurrection. God said to him: Then you are one of those whose destruction I have delayed until the appointed time for the destruction of all My creation, and that is when there will not remain on the earth any dwellings of the children of Adam.
15:39: God Almighty said: He said, ‘My Lord, because You have put me in error, I will surely make [disobedience] attractive to them on earth, and I will mislead them all.’
15:40: God the Most High says: Iblis said, My Lord, because You have misled me by Your misleading, I will surely make attractive to them on the earth, and it is as if his saying because You have misled me was taken in the form of an oath, as one says: By God, or by the might of God, I will mislead them. And what He meant by His saying: I will surely make attractive to them on the earth is that I will make Your disobedience attractive to them, and I will make it beloved to them on the earth. And I will mislead them all, meaning: and I will lead them astray from the path of right guidance. Except for Your chosen servants among them, meaning: except for those whom You have chosen by Your guidance and guided, for that is someone over whom I have no authority nor power. And it has been read: except for those whom You have chosen, so whoever reads it in this way means: except for those who are sincere in their obedience to You, for I have no power over them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: Except for Your chosen servants among them, meaning: the believers. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Amr told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, Except for Your chosen servants among them, Qatada said: This is the dual meaning of God, may He be exalted.
15:41: God Almighty said: He said, 'This is a straight path to Me.'
15:42: The readers differed in their reading of his statement, He said, ‘This is a straight path to me.’ The majority of the readers of Hijaz, Medina, Kufa, and Basra read it as, This is a straight path to me, meaning: This is a straight path to me. So the meaning of the statement was: This is a path that leads back to Me. So I will reward everyone for their deeds, as God Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. This is similar to what someone says to someone who threatens and intimidates him: Your path is upon me, and I am upon your path. So too is his statement: This is a path, meaning: This is a path upon Me and this is a path to Me. This is the interpretation of whoever reads it in this way. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told me, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, all of them on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: This is the path of Ali, which is straight, he said: The truth returns to God, and its path is upon Him, it does not deviate from anything. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Ahmad bin Yusuf told us: Al-Qasim told us: Marwan bin Shuja’ told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ziyad bin Abi Maryam and Abdullah bin Katheer, that they read it: This is the straight path of Ali, and they said: Ali is to me and is in their position. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated to us: Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail bin Muslim, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: This is the straight path of Ali, meaning: straight to me. Qais bin Abbad, Ibn Sirin, and Qatada read this, according to what was reported from them: This is the straight path of Ali, with Ali in the nominative case, as an attribute of the path, meaning: high. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said: Jaafar Al-Basri told me, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, that he used to recite: This is Ali’s straight path, meaning: high. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: This is a straight path to me, meaning high and straight. Bishr said, Yazid said, Saeed said: This is how we and Qatada read it. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Abdul-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Abu Al-Awam, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Qais bin Abbad: This is the straight path of Ali, meaning: lofty. The correct reading of this, according to us, is the reading of those who read, This is the straight path of Ali, according to the interpretation that we mentioned from Mujahid and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and those who agreed with them on it, due to the consensus of the proof of the reciters on it, and the anomaly of what contradicted it. And His statement: Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them, except for those who follow you of the deviators, God Almighty says: Indeed, My servants - you have no argument over them, except for those who follow you in what you called their father of misguidance, of those who have gone astray and perished. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwaid told us, he said: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Muhab, he said: Yazid bin Qusayt told us, he said: “The prophets had mosques outside their villages, so if the prophet wanted to ask his Lord about something, he would go to his mosque, pray as much as God had written for him, then ask whatever he wanted, and while the prophet was in his mosque, the enemy of God came and sat between him and the qiblah, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan, so the enemy of God said: Do you see the one from whom you sought refuge? It is he, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan, and he repeated that three times, so the enemy of God said: Tell me by what means you will be saved from me, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather tell me by what means you will overcome the son of Adam, twice, so each one of them took on the other, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, the Most High, says: ‘Indeed, over My servants you have no authority except those who follow you of the deviators,’ the enemy of God said: I heard this before you were born, The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty says: (But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.) And by God, I never felt anything from you except that I sought refuge in God from you. So the enemy of God said: You have spoken the truth in this, so you will be saved from me. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So tell me, by what you overcome the son of Adam? He said: I overcome it when I am angry and when I am in a state of desire.
15:43: God Almighty says: And Hell is their promised destination, all of them.
15:44: God Almighty says to Satan: “And Hell is the promised place for those who follow you, all together. It has seven gates.” He says: Hell has seven levels, and for each level there is a portion of Satan’s followers, meaning a divided portion and share. He mentioned that the gates of Hell are layers, one above the other. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us: I heard Abu Harun al-Ghanawi: I heard Hattan: I heard Ali while he was giving a sermon, he said: The gates of Hell are like this. And Shu`bah placed one hand on the other. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Harun al-Ghanawi, on the authority of Hattan ibn Abdullah, he said: Ali said: Do you know what the gates of Hell are like? We said: Yes, like these gates. He said: No, but they are like this. So Abu Harun described layers, one on top of the other, and Abu Bishr did the same. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Harun al-Ghanawi, on the authority of Hattan bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ali, who said: Do you know how the gates of Hell are? They said: Like these gates. He said: No, but like this, and he described some of them above others. Harun bin Ishaq told us: Mus`ab bin Al-Muqaddam told us: Israel told us: Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Hubayrah, on the authority of Ali, who said: The gates of Hell are seven, one above the other. The first will be filled, then the second, then the third, then all of them will be filled. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Shababah told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Hubayrah, on the authority of Ali, who said: The gates of Hell are seven, one above the other, and he pointed with his fingers to the first, then the second, then the third until they are all filled. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Yunus bin Abi Ishaq told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hubayrah bin Yarim, who said: I heard Ali say: The gates of Hell are one above the other, so the first one is filled, then the one next to it, until the end of it. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said: Ali told us, he said: Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Wasiti told us, on the authority of Jahdam, he said: I heard Ikrimah say regarding His statement: It has seven doors, he said: It has seven floors. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: It has seven gates, he said: The first of them is Hell, then Laza, then Al-Hutama, then Al-Sa’ir, then Saqar, then Al-Jahim, then Al-Hawiyah. And in Hell is Abu Jahl. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: It has seven gates, for each gate there is a portion allotted. And by God, they are dwellings according to their deeds.
15:45: God Almighty says: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs.
15:46: God Almighty says: "Enter it in peace, secure."
15:47: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who feared God by obeying Him and feared Him, and avoided His disobedience, will be in gardens and springs. It will be said to them: “Enter it in peace, secure” from the punishment of God, or from being deprived of a blessing that God has bestowed upon you, and an honor with which He has honored you. His statement, And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment, means: And We will remove whatever is in the hearts of these righteous people whose characteristics He has described of rancor and malice toward one another. The people of interpretation differed about the state in which God removes that from their hearts. Some of them said: He removes that after they enter Paradise. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Ghassan told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Bishr al-Basri, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Umamah, he said: The people of Paradise will enter Paradise with whatever was in their hearts in this world of rancor and grudges, until when they meet and meet, God will remove whatever rancor was in their hearts in this world. Then he recited: And We will remove whatever rancor was in their hearts. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Fadala told us, on the authority of Luqman, on the authority of Abu Umamah, he said: A believer will not enter Paradise until God removes from their hearts any rancor, then removes from them the ferocious beast. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Musa, he heard Al-Hasan Al-Basri say: Ali said: By God, it was about us, the people of Badr, that the verse was revealed: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [while] they will be brothers, on thrones facing each other. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah: And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment, he said: of enmity. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Wasiti told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak: And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment, he said: enmity. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ali: And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment, he said: enmity. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Ibn Jarmuz, the killer of Al-Zubayr, came to Ali asking permission to see him. Ali kept him away for a long time, then he gave him permission and said to him: As for the people of affliction, you are avoiding them! Ali said: May the dust be in your mouth. I hope that Talhah, Al-Zubayr, and I will be among those of whom God said: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment i.e., injury or loss, [while] they will be brothers facing each other on thrones. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Ali, something similar. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Abaan bin Abdullah Al-Bajali, on the authority of Na’eem bin Abi And, on the authority of Rab’i bin Harash, in a similar manner: And he added to it: He said: Then a man from Hamdan stood up to Ali and said: God is more just than that, O Commander of the Faithful. He said: Then Ali shouted a shout that made me think that the palace was collapsing because of it, then he said: If it is not us, then who are they? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated: Abu Muawiyah the blind narrated: Abu Malik al-Ashja’i narrated: Abu Habeeba, a freed slave of Talhah, said: Imran bin Talhah entered upon Ali after he had finished with the Companions of the Camel. He welcomed him and said: I hope that God will make me and your father among those about whom God said: Brothers on thrones facing each other. Two men were sitting on one side of the carpet and said: God is more just than that. You killed them yesterday and you become brothers? Ali said: People who are the most distant and most crushing land. Who are they then if it is not me and Talhah? Abu Muawiyah narrated the hadith to us in full. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Affan told us: Abdul Wahid told us: Abu Malik told us: Abu Habeeba told us: Ali said to Ibn Talha: I hope that God will make me and your father among those from whose hearts God has removed any rancor, and will make us brothers facing each other on thrones. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Hammad bin Khalid Al-Khayyat told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Juwairiyah, who said: Muawiyah bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Imran bin Talha: When Ali looked at me, he said: Welcome, my nephew, and he mentioned something similar. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Yazid bin Harun told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: Al-Ashtar asked permission to see Ali while Ibn Talhah was with him, so he detained him, then he gave him permission, and when he entered he said: I see that you have only detained me for this, he said: Yes, he said: I see that if you had Uthman’s son you would have detained me, he said: Yes, I hope that Uthman and I will be among those of whom God said: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [so that] they will be brothers, facing each other on thrones. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Ishaq Al-Arzaq told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, something similar. Al-Hasan told us: Yaqub bin Ishaq Al-Hadrami told us: Al-Sakn bin Al-Mughira told us: Muawiyah bin Rushd told us: Ali said: I hope that Uthman and I will be among those of whom God said: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [while] they will be brothers facing each other on thrones. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Ibn al-Mutawakkil al-Naji told us, that Abu Saeed al-Khudri told them that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The believers will be saved from the Fire and detained on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and some of them will exact retribution from others for wrongs that were committed between them in the world, until when they are refined and purified, they will be permitted to enter Paradise.” He said: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of them will be guided to his home in Paradise more than to his home that he had in the world. Some of them said: They are only likened to the people of Friday who have returned from their Friday prayer. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Affan bin Muslim narrated to us, he said: Yazid bin Zari’ narrated to us, he said: Saeed bin Abi Arubah narrated to us regarding this verse: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [while] they will be brothers facing each other on thrones, he said: Qatada narrated to us that Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji narrated to them that Abu Saeed al-Khudri narrated to them, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar to it, until His saying: And they will be permitted to enter Paradise,” then he made the rest of the speech from Qatada, he said: Qatada said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, one of them is more guided in his home, then he mentioned the rest of the hadith similar to the hadith of Bishr, except that the speech to the end is from Qatada, except that he said in his hadith: Qatada said and some of them said: They are not likened to anyone except the people of Friday when they leave Friday. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi narrated to me, he said: Omar bin Zur’ah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Zubaidi, on the authority of Kathir Al-Nawa, he said: I heard him say: I entered upon Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ali, and I said: My guardian is your guardian, my peace is your peace, my enemy is your enemy, and my war is your war. I ask you by God, do I disavow Abu Bakr and Umar? He said: Then I have gone astray and I am not among the guided ones. Befriend them, Kathir, and whatever you find is upon my neck. Then he recited this verse: Brothers on thrones facing each other, meaning: brothers who face each other, not turning their backs to each other and looking at the back of their necks. And this is how the people of interpretation interpreted it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us: Hisin told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: On thrones facing each other, he said: One of them should not look at the back of his companion. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya, Abd al-Rahman and Muammal told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. As-Sirr is the plural of Sarir, just as al-Jadid is the plural of Jadid. He made the plural of Surran and made the doubling clear in it, and the two Ra’s are mobile due to the lightness of the nouns, and you do not do that in verbs due to the weight of the verbs, but they assimilate them into the verb so that one of the two letters is still and thus it is lightened, and if something enters the verb that makes the second still, they make it appear doubling in that case.
15:48: God Almighty says: No fatigue will touch them therein, nor will they be expelled from it.
15:49: God Almighty says: Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
15:50: God the Almighty says: These righteous people, whose description He has described in Paradise, will not be touched by fatigue, meaning exhaustion, nor will they be expelled from it, meaning: They will not be expelled from Paradise and its delights and what God has given them in it, but that will be permanent forever. And His statement: Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful, God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Inform My servants, O Muhammad, that I am the One who conceals their sins if they repent from them and return, by not disgracing them for them and punishing them for them, the Most Merciful towards them, that I will punish them after they repent from them for them: And that My punishment is the painful punishment, meaning: And inform them also that My punishment for those who persist in their sins, persist in them and do not repent from them, is the painful punishment that no other punishment resembles. This is from God a warning to His creation to proceed with His sins, and a command from Him to them to return and repent. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment, he said: It has reached us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If the servant knew the extent of God’s forgiveness, he would not refrain from doing something forbidden, and if he knew the extent of His punishment, he would despise himself. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Ibn Al-Makki told us, he said: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said: Mus`ab bin Thabit told us, he said: Asim bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Rabah, “on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us from the door through which the Banu Shaybah enter, and he said: Do I not see you laughing? Then he turned away until he was at the Black Stone, then he came back to us, and he said: When I went out, Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, came back and said: O Muhammad, God says: Why do you make My servants despair? O my servants, I am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful, and My punishment is the most painful punishment.”
15:51: God Almighty said: And tell them about the guests of Abraham.
15:52: God Almighty said: “When they entered upon him and said, ‘Peace,’ he said, ‘Indeed, we are afraid of you.’”
15:53: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And inform My servants, O Muhammad, about the guests of Abraham, meaning the angels who entered upon Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, when their Lord sent them to the people of Lot to destroy them. “And they said, ‘Peace.’” That is, the guest said to Abraham: “Peace.” He said, ‘Indeed, we are afraid of you.’ That is, Abraham said: Indeed, we are afraid. We have already explained the reason for the accusative in His statement “Peace,” and the reason for Abraham’s fear of his guest, and the differences of those who differed, and we have provided evidence for the correct statement about it in what has passed before, so that there is no need to repeat it in this place. As for His statement “They said, ‘Peace,’” meaning the guest, he has collected the report about them, and they are in one word, because the guest is a name for one, two, and a group, like weight, diameter, and justice, so he collected its report, and it is one word. And his saying, They said, ‘Do not delay,’ means: The guest said to Abraham, Do not delay, do not be afraid, We give you good tidings of a learned boy.
15:54: God Almighty says: Abraham said to the angels who gave him the good report of a learned boy, “You have given me good report even though old age has touched me. With what do you give me good report?” He says: With what do you give me good report? Mujahid used to say about this: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: “He said: Do you give me good tidings even though old age has touched me? So with what do you give me good tidings?” He said: He was amazed at his old age and the old age of his wife. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly, and he said: On the condition that old age has touched me, and its meaning is: because old age has touched me and that old age has touched me, and it is similar to his saying It is true that I do not say about God except the truth meaning: that I do not say, and he represents it in speech: I came to you that you give, but I did not find you giving.
15:55: God Almighty said: They said, ‘We have given you good tidings in truth, so do not be among the despairing.’
15:56: God Almighty says: Abraham's guest said to him: We have given you good tidings of certain truth and knowledge from us that God has bestowed upon you a learned boy, so do not be among those who despair of God's grace, and lose hope in Him, but be glad with what We have given you good tidings of and accept the good tidings. The readers differed in reading his statement: from the despairing ones. The majority of the readers of the regions read it: from the despairing ones with an alif. It was mentioned on the authority of Yahya bin Waththab that he used to read it as the despairing ones. The correct reading in this regard is what the readers of the countries have said, due to the consensus of the authorities on this, and the anomaly of what contradicts it. And His saying: And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those who are astray? God Almighty says: Abraham said to the guest: And who despairs of the mercy of God except the people who have strayed from the path of truth, and abandoned the right path in their abandonment of hope in God, and he who hopes in Him is not disappointed, and thus they have strayed from the religion of God. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement: And whoever despairs. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited And whoever despairs with a fatha on the noon except for Al-A'mash and Al-Kisa'i, who both broke the noon of Yaquntu. As for those who opened the noon of it from those we mentioned, they recited: Min ba'd ma yaqantu with a fatha on the qaf and the noon. As for Al-A'mash, he used to recite it: Min ba'd ma yaqantu with a kasra on the noon. Al-Kisa'i used to recite it with a fatha on the noon. Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala' used to recite both letters in the manner that we mentioned from Al-Kisa'i's recitation. The most correct reading in this regard is the reading of those who read min ba’d ma qan’tu with a fatha on the nun and man yaqantu with a kasra on the nun, because the authoritative readers have agreed to open it in his statement min ba’d ma qan’tu. So closing it in man yaqantu is more appropriate, since there was agreement to open it in qantu, because if the verb is determined by it with a fatha, and it is not one of the six throat letters, then it is in yaf’ul with a kasra or a damma. As for opening, this is not known in the speech of the Arabs.
15:57: God Almighty said: He said, ‘What is the matter with you, O messengers?’
15:58: God Almighty said: They said, ‘Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals.’
15:59: God Almighty said: "Except the family of Lot. Indeed, We will save them all."
15:60: God the Almighty says: Abraham said to the angels: What is your affair? What is your command, O messengers? The angels said to him: We have been sent to a people of criminals. He says: To a people who have acquired disbelief in God, except for the family of Lot: He says: Except for the followers of Lot in the religion that he is upon, for We will not destroy them, but We will save them from the punishment with which We were commanded to punish the people of Lot, except for the wife of Lot, whom We determined to be among those who remain behind. He says: God decreed concerning her that she was among those who remain, then she is destroyed after that. We have explained the past with its evidence.
15:61: God Almighty said: So when the messengers came to the family of Lot.
15:62: God Almighty said: He said, 'Indeed, you are a people who deny.'
15:63: God Almighty says: When the messengers of God came to the family of Lot, Lot did not recognize them and said to them: You are a people who are unknown. That is, we do not recognize you. The messengers said to him: Rather, we are messengers of God who have come to you with what your people were doubting would befall them of God's punishment for their disbelief in Him. Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told me: Shababah told us: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq told us: Abdullah told us, all on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: “He said: You are a people who deny,” he said: Lot denied them. And His statement: Because of what they were in doubt about, he said: About the punishment of the people of Lot. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.
15:64: God Almighty says: And We have brought you the truth, and indeed, We are truthful.
15:65: God the Almighty says: The messengers said to Lot: We have brought you the certain truth from God. That truth is the punishment with which God punished the people of Lot. Their story and tales were mentioned in Surah Hud and elsewhere when God sent His messengers to punish them with it. And their saying: And indeed, we are truthful means: We are truthful in what we told you, O Lot, that God will destroy your people. So set out with your family during a part of the night God the Almighty says, informing us about His messengers that they said to Lot: Set out with your family during a part of the night, and follow, O Lot, the backs of your family with whom you set out, and be behind them, and set out behind them while they are in front of you, and let none of you look back, and go where God commands you. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Warqa’, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And let none of you turn back, let none of you turn behind him, nor let him ascend. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: And let none of you turn back, means no one should look behind him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And follow their backs, he said: He was commanded to be behind his family, following their backs at the end of them when they walked. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Then set out with your family during a part of the night, he said: part of al-Layl 92:and follow their backs, he said: the backs of his family.
15:66: God Almighty said: “And We decreed for him that matter: that the root of these people would be cut off by morning.”
15:67: God the Almighty says: And We completed that matter to Lot, and We revealed that their descendants would be cut off in the morning. He says: The last of your people and the first of them will be cut off and uprooted in the morning of their night. And that from His saying that their descendants is in the accusative case in response to the command to bring about the end of it. It may be permissible for it to be in the accusative case due to the loss of the preposition, and its meaning would be: And We decreed that matter to him, that the descendants of these people would be cut off in the morning. And it was mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah: And We said that the descendants of these people would be cut off in the morning. And what he meant by His saying: in the morning is when they became, or when they become. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said, his statement: Their last remains will be cut off in the morning means: their destruction will be eradicated in the morning. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And We decreed that matter to him, he said: We revealed to him. And his saying, And the people of the city came, rejoicing, means: And the people of the city of Sodom, who were the people of Lot, came when they heard that a guest had hosted Lot, rejoicing at their arrival in their city, hoping to commit an immoral act. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And the people of Medina came, rejoicing, they were rejoicing at the guests of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Lot, when they came down to them because they wanted to come to them with the evil.
15:68: God Almighty said: He said, ‘These are my guests, so do not disgrace me.’
15:69: God Almighty says: And fear God and do not be disgraced.
15:70: God the Almighty says: Lot said to his al-Nas 114:These people whom you have come to, seeking immorality from them, are my guests, and it is the duty of a man to honor his guest, so do not disgrace yourselves, O people, in my presence, and honor me by refraining from exposing them to harm. And His statement: And fear God means: And fear God in me and in yourselves, lest His punishment befall you. And do not disgrace means: And do not humiliate me or degrade me in front of them, by exposing them to harm. “They said: Did We not forbid you from hosting anyone from the worlds?” God the Almighty says: Lot’s people said: Did We not forbid you from hosting anyone from the worlds? As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Did We not forbid you from the worlds? He said: Did We not forbid you from hosting anyone?
15:71: God Almighty said: "He said, 'These are my daughters, if you are going to do something.'
15:72: God Almighty said: By your life, they are in their intoxication, wandering blindly.
15:73: God Almighty says: Lot said to his al-Nas 114:Marry women and have intercourse with them, but do not do what God has forbidden you of having intercourse with men, if you are going to do what I command you to do and abide by my command. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “He said: These are my daughters, if you are to do something.” The Prophet of God, Lot, ordered them to marry women, and he wanted to protect his guests with his daughters. And His saying: By your life, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: By your life, O Muhammad, your people from Quraysh are wandering blindly in their intoxication, meaning: they are wandering in their misguidance and ignorance. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said: Saeed bin Zaid told us, he said: Amr bin Malik told us, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God did not create, nor did He sow, nor did He bring into being a soul more honorable to God than Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I did not hear God swear by the life of anyone other than him. God Almighty said, By your life, they are in their intoxication, wandering blindly. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Yaqub bin Ishaq Al-Hadrami told us: Al-Hasan bin Abi Ja`far told us: Amr bin Malik told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza`, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God: By your life, indeed, in their intoxication, they are wandering blindly. He said: God Almighty did not swear by the life of anyone except by the life of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: By your life, O Muhammad, and your life and your remaining in this world, Indeed, they are in their intoxication, wandering blindly. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: By your life, they are in their intoxication, wandering blindly. This is a word from the speech of the Arabs. In their intoxication means they are in their misguidance, wandering blindly, meaning they are playing. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: I asked Al-A’mash about his statement: By your life, they are in their intoxication, wandering blindly. He said: In their heedlessness, they are wandering. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding their drunkenness. He said: In their misguidance, they are playing. He said: They are playing. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Mujahid said: They wander blindly meaning: they hesitate. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: By your life means: by your life, Indeed, they are in their intoxication, wandering blindly he said: they persist. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: They disliked a man saying: By my life, as they considered it to be like saying: By my life. And His statement: So the blast seized them at sunrise. God Almighty says: So the thunderbolt of punishment, which is the blast, seized them at sunrise. He says: When they shone, and its meaning is: When the sun rose. The accusative of shirkīn and sabhīn is in the state of if they became morning. And when they shone, it is said from it: They were shouted at: when they were destroyed. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Then the blast overtook them at sunrise, he said: when the sun rose, that was at sunrise.
15:74: God Almighty said: So We turned it upside down and rained down upon them stones of baked clay.
15:75: God Almighty says: So We turned the upper part of their land into the lower part, and We rained down upon them stones of baked clay. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us: on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah: And We rained down upon them stones of baked clay, meaning of clay. And His statement: Indeed in that are signs for those who take signs. He says: Indeed in what We did to the people of Lot by destroying them and inflicting upon them the punishment are signs and indications for those who take into consideration and consider the signs of God, and a lesson on the consequences of the actions of those who disobey Him and disbelieve in Him. And what He, the Most High, means by that are the people of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Quraysh. He says: So your people, O Muhammad, in the people of Lot, and what befell them of God’s punishment when they denied their Messenger and persisted in their error and misguidance, is a lesson. And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying: for those who see, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Abdul-A’la bin Wasil told me: Ya’la bin Ubaid told us: Abdul-Malik bin Abi Sulayman told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Indeed in that are signs for those who take signs, he said: for those who reflect. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, and al-Hasan al-Za’farani told us: Muhammad ibn Ubayd told me: Abd al-Malik told me, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed in that are signs for those who take signs. He said: For those who take signs. Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us. Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us: Shababah told us: Warqa’ told us. Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shibl told us. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Usamah told us: Shibl told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The ones who see things with their own eYa-Sin 36:the ones who discern. He said: I saw good in you as a voluntary act. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Qays, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed in that are signs for those who take signs. He said: Those who take signs. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed in that are signs for those who take signs, meaning: for those who observe. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Muhammad ibn Yazid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: For those who observe he said for those who look. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed in that are signs for those who take signs: that is, for those who consider. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: For those who take signs, he said: For those who consider. Muhammad ibn Amara told me: Hasan ibn Malik told me: Muhammad ibn Kathir told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Qays, on the authority of Atiyya, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of the insight of the believer, for he sees with the light of God. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed in that are signs for those who reflect. Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Tusi told us: Muhammad bin Katheer, a client of Banu Hashim, told us: Amr bin Qais al-Mala’i told us, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Tusi told me: al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: al-Furat bin al-Sa’ib told us: Maimun bin Mihran told us, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of the insight of the believer, for the believer sees with the light of God. Abdul-A’la bin Wasil told us: Saeed bin Muhammad Al-Jarmi told us: Abdul-Wahid bin Wasil told us: Abu Bishr Al-Mazlaq told us, on the authority of Thabit Al-Bunani, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has servants who know people by their appearance. Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed in that are signs for those who reflect, he said: Those who ponder and consider, who reflect on things, think about them, and consider. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: for those who see, he said: for those who look. Abu Sharhabil al-Himsi told me: Sulayman ibn Salamah told us: al-Mu’ammal ibn Sa’id ibn Yusuf al-Rahbi told us: Abu al-Mu’alla Asad ibn Wada’ah al-Ta’i told us: Wahb ibn Munabbih told us, on the authority of Tawus ibn Kaysan, on the authority of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of the insight of the believer, for he sees with the light of God and speaks with God’s guidance.
15:76: God Almighty says: And indeed, it is a straight path.
15:77: God Almighty says: And indeed, this city, the city of Sodom, is on a clear, established road that anyone passing by can see, there is nothing hidden about it, and it does not move from its place, so the one with a sound mind is ignorant of its matter, and the consequences of disobeying God and disbelieving in Him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us: Shababah told us: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq told us: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, and Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And indeed, it is on a straight path, he said: On a marked path. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And it is on a clear path, meaning: on a clear path. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And indeed, it is a straight path, he said: A road. The path: the road. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: On a fixed path, he said: On a marked path. And His statement: Indeed in that is a sign for the believers. God Almighty says: Indeed in what We did to the people of Lot, what We did to them, is a clear sign and indication for whoever believes in God of His vengeance on the people who disbelieve in Him, and His rescue from His punishment, if it befalls a people among them who believe in Him. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Saeed bin Jeer, regarding his statement: Indeed in that is a sign, he said: It is like a man saying to his family: The sign between me and you is that I will send you my ring, or such and such a sign. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed in that is a sign. He said: Do you not see a man sending his ring to his family and saying: Bring it, take it, bring it, take it? So when they see it, they know that it is true.
15:78: God Almighty said: And indeed, the companions of the thicket were wrongdoers.
15:79: God Almighty says: And the companions of the thicket were wrongdoers. He says: They were disbelievers in God. The thicket is the intertwined, crowded trees, as Umayyah said: The pigeons cooed on the fur of the thicket on the branch wings And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told us: Atab bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Khasif, who said: His statement: The people of the thicket, he said: the trees, and they used to eat fresh fruit in the summer, and dry fruit in the winter. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And indeed, the companions of the thicket were wrongdoers, he told us that they were people of a thicket. Most of their trees were this doom tree, and their messenger, as far as we have been informed, was Shu’ayb, peace be upon him. He was sent to them and to the people of Madyan. He was sent to two nations of people, and they were punished with two different punishments. As for the people of Madyan, the blast overtook them, and as for the companions of the thicket, they were people of trees that were overlapping each other. He told us that the heat was imposed upon them for seven days, during which no shade would shade them, and nothing would protect them from it. Then God sent a cloud upon them, and they settled beneath it seeking refreshment in it, so God made it a punishment for them. He sent fire upon them, and it blazed upon them and consumed them. That is the punishment of the Day of the Shade. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said: Amr ibn Thabit told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, he said: The companions of the thicket: the companions of the thicket. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, his statement: And indeed, the companions of the thicket were wrongdoers, he said: The people of Shu’ayb. Ibn Abbas said: The thicket had thickets and trees in it that they were in. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, in his statement: The Companions of the Thicket, he said: They are the people of Shu`ayb, and the thicket is the thicket. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Hilal, on the authority of Amr ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Qatada, that he said: The companions of the thicket, and the thicket is the intertwined tree. And His saying: So We took vengeance upon them, and indeed, they were in a clear sign. God Almighty says: So We took vengeance upon the oppressors of the companions of the thicket. And His statement: And indeed, they are on a clear path, meaning: And indeed, the city of the Companions of the Thicket, and the city of the people of Lot. And the ha’ and the mim in His statement: And indeed, they are from the mention of the two cities, on a clear path, meaning: a path that they follow in their journey, and are guided by, clear, meaning: it shows the straightness of the path to whoever follows it. And the path was made an imam because it is followed and followed. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And indeed, they are on a clear path, meaning: on the road. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: So We took vengeance on them, and indeed, they were in a clear path. He said: An apparent path. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: And indeed, they are on a clear path, he said: On a marked path.
