Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Ubaid Abu Zaid told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: The Qur’an is repeated, and so are Surat Al-Baqarah, Al Imran, An-Nisa, Al-Ma’idah, Al-An’am, Al-A’raf, and Bara’ah. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, and on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said: The entire Qur’an is repeated. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Mathani: what is repeated from the Qur’an. Have you not heard the statement of God Almighty, “God has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book, repeated.” It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Al-Mathani is the Qur’an. God mentions the same story repeatedly, and this is His saying: He has sent down the best statement as a consistent Book, repeated in pairs. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by the seven oft-repeated verses are the seven verses that are the verses of the Mother of the Book, due to the authenticity of the report on this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who: Yazid bin Mukhallad bin Khidash Al-Wasiti told me: Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Mother of the Qur’an is the seven oft-repeated verses that I was given. Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam al-Ajli told me: Yazid ibn Zurai’ told us: Ruh ibn al-Qasim told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to my father: ‘I would like to teach you a surah the like of which has not been revealed in the Torah, the Gospel, or the Criterion.’ He said: ‘Yes, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘I hope that you will not leave this door until you have learned it.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took my hand and spoke to me, but I kept slowing down for fear that I would reach the door before the conversation was over. When I came close, I said: ‘O Messenger of God, what is the surah that you promised me?’ He said: ‘What do you recite in prayer?’ So I recited to him the Mother of the Qur’an. He said: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, nothing like it has been revealed in the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, or the Criterion. It is the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an that I have been given.” Abu Kuraib narrated: Zaid bin Habbab Al-Akli narrated: Malik bin Anas narrated: Al-Ala bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Ya’qub, a freed slave of Urwah, informed me on the authority of Abu Saeed, a freed slave of Amir bin so-and-so, or the son of so-and-so, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: When you begin the prayer, what do you begin it with? He said: Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds, until he concluded it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an that you have been given. Abu Kurayb narrated: Abu Usamah narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Ja`far bin Al-`Ala` bin Abdul Rahman bin Ya`qub, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of my father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not teach you a surah the like of which has not been revealed in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Criterion? I said: Yes. He said: I hope that you will not leave that door until you learn it. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and I stood up with him, and he began to talk to me with his hand in mine, so I began to delay, not wanting him to leave before he told me about it. When he came near the door, I said: O Messenger of God, the surah that you promised me! He said: How do you recite it when you begin the prayer? He said: So he recited the Opening of the Book, and he said: It is it, and it is the seven oft-repeated verses about which God, the Most High, said: And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an which has been given to you. Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Al-Fadl Al-Madani, on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The two rak’ahs in which one does not recite are like a premature baby who has not been completed. A man said: What if I only have the Mother of the Qur’an? He said: “It is sufficient for you. It is the Mother of the Qur’an, it is the seven oft-repeated verses.” Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, on the authority of al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The rak’ah in which one does not recite is like a premature baby. I said to Abu Hurayrah: And if I only have the Mother of the Qur’an with me? He said: “It is sufficient for you. It is the Mother of the Book, the Mother of the Qur’an, and the Seven Oft-Repeated.” Abu Kuraib told me: Khalid bin Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ja`far, on the authority of Al-`Ala` bin `Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, God has not revealed in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Criterion anything like it - meaning the Mother of the Qur’an - and it is the seven oft-repeated verses that God Almighty has given me.” Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Abi Tha’lab told me, on the authority of Sa’id Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: It is the mother of the Qur’an, it is the opening of the Book, and it is the seven oft-repeated verses. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Yazid bin Harun and Shababah told us: Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, on the authority of Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the opening of the Book, he said: It is the opening of the Book, and it is the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an.” Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Affan narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman bin Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Al-Ala narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his father Hurairah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by Ubayy bin Ka’b and said: ‘Would you like me to teach you a surah the like of which has not been revealed in the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, or the Criterion?’ I said: ‘Yes, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘How do you recite in prayer?’ So I recited to him Umm al-Kitab, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no surah has been revealed in the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, or the Criterion like it. It is the Seven Oft-Repeated and the Great Qur’an.’” Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated: Wahb bin Jarir narrated: Saeed bin Habib narrated: Hafs bin Asim narrated: Abu Saeed bin Al-Mualla narrated: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him while he was praying, so he prayed, then he came to him and said: What prevented you from answering me? He said: I was praying. He said: Didn’t God say: ‘O you who believe, respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life’? He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will teach you the greatest Surah in the Qur’an. It was as if he had explained it or had forgotten, so I said: O Messenger of God, what did you say? He said: ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. It is the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an that I have been given.’” If the correct interpretation of this is what we said about the one we cited as evidence, then what is necessary is that the word Mathani refers to the entire Qur’an, so the meaning of the statement is: And We have given you seven verses, some of which repeat others. If this is the case, then Mathani is the plural of Mathna, and the verses of the Qur’an are described as such, because some of them repeat others, and some of them follow others with chapters separating them, so the end of a verse and the beginning of the next one are known, as the Most High described it when He said: God has sent down the best statement, a consistent Book, repeated, from which the skins of those who fear their Lord shiver. It is possible that its meaning is as Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said. Whoever said this is that the Qur’an is called Mathani because the stories and report are repeated in it time after time. We have already mentioned the statement of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that it is called Mathani because it is repeated in every recitation. Ibn Abbas said: It was called Mathani because God Almighty mentioned it excepted it for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and not for all the other prophets besides him, so He saved it for him. Some Arab scholars claim that it was called Mathani because it contains the phrase the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful twice, and that it is repeated in every surah, meaning: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. As for the statement that we chose in interpreting that, it is one of the statements of Ibn Abbas, and it is the statement of Tawus, Mujahid, and Abu Malik, and we mentioned that before. As for his saying, And the Great Qur’an, the Qur’an is connected to the seven, meaning: We have given you seven verses of the Qur’an, and other than that from the rest of the Qur’an. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And the Great Qur’an, he said: The rest of it, meaning the rest of the Qur’an with the seven oft-repeated verses. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the Great Qur’an, meaning: the entire Book.
15:88: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not wish, O Muhammad, for what We have made of the adornments of this world as a provision for the rich among your people, who do not believe in God and the Last Day, to enjoy it, for there is a severe punishment behind them. And do not grieve over them. He says: Do not grieve over what they have enjoyed, so hasten for them, for in the Hereafter you will have something better than it, along with what We have hastened for you in this world of honor by giving you the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an. It is said from this: So-and-so extended his eye to so-and-so’s money: if he desired it, wished for it, and wanted it. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah that he used to interpret this verse as the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He is not one of us who does not chant the Qur’an meaning, he who is not satisfied with it. And he said: Do you not see him say: “And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an. Do not strain your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them”? So he ordered him to be satisfied with the Qur’an instead of money. He said: And from this is the saying of another: Whoever is given the Qur’an, and sees that someone has been given better than what he has been given, then he has magnified what is small and belittled what is great. And similar to what we said about His statement, pairs, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them: the rich, like-minded, similar. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, he said: It forbids a man from wishing for his companion’s money. And His statement, And lower your wing to the believers, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Be gentle with those who believe in you, follow you and your words, and bring them close to you, and do not be harsh with them, and do not be rough with them. God Almighty commands him to be gentle with the believers. The two wings of the children of Adam are his sides, and the two wings are the two sides, and from this is the statement of God Almighty: And put your hand to your side It was said: Its meaning is: to your side and your side.
15:89: God Almighty says: And say, 'Indeed, I am the clear warner.'
15:90: God Almighty says: As We sent down to those who divided.
15:91: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists: I am the warner who has made clear his warning to you of the calamity and punishment that will be sent down upon you from God for your persistence in your error, just as We sent down upon those who divided it up, meaning: Like the calamity and punishment that God Almighty sent down upon those who divided up the Qur’an, making it into two parts. Then the people of interpretation differed about those who were meant by his saying those who divided, so some of them said: He meant by it: the Jews and Christians, and he said: Their division was that they divided the Qur’an and its parts, so they believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. Who said that? Isa bin Othman Al-Ramli told me: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, As We sent down upon those who divided the Qur’an into parts, he said: They are the Jews and Christians, they believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. Abu Kuraib and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us: Hisham told us: Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, As We sent down to those who divided the Qur’an into parts, he said: They are the People of the Book, they divided it and made it into parts, so they believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: As We sent down upon the dividers * Who divided the Qur’an into parts, he said: Those who believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Those who divide are the People of the Book who have divided the Qur’an into parts meaning: they believe in some of it and disbelieve in some of it. Matar bin Muhammad Al-Dhabi told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, he said: Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, that he said regarding His statement: As We sent down to those who divided, he said: They are the People of the Book. Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, that he said regarding this verse, As We sent down upon those who divided the Qur’an into parts, he said: They are the People of the Book who believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Those who have divided the Qur’an into parts, he said: They are the People of the Book, they divided it and made it into parts, so they believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: They cut it up and made it into parts like the parts of a camel. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: They are the People of the Book. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, As We sent down to those who divided, he said: They are the Jews and Christians from the People of the Book, who divided the Book and made it into parts, meaning: parties, so they believed in some and disbelieved in some. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Those who divided believed in some, disbelieved in some, and divided the Book. Others said, Al-Muqtasimiyyun: the People of the Book, but they were called Al-Muqtasimiyyun because some of them said, mocking the Qur’an: This surah is mine, and some of them said: This is mine. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of `Ikrimah, that he said regarding this verse, Those who have divided the Qur’an into parts, he said: They were mocking, one saying: I have Surat al-Baqarah, and another saying: I have Surat Al-`Imran. Others said: They are the People of the Book, but they were called: the dividers, because they divided their books and divided them up by some of them believing in some of them and disbelieving in others, and others disbelieving in what others believed in, and believing in what others disbelieved in. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Mujahid: As We sent down upon those who divided the Qur’an into parts. He said: They are the Jews and Christians. They divided their book, separated it, and made it into parts. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told me, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: As We sent down to those who divided he said: The People of the Book divided it and changed it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: As We sent down to those who divided he said: The People of the Book. Others said: He meant by that a group of the infidels of Quraysh, specifically. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: As We sent down to the dividers * Who divided the Qur’an into parts means a group of five from Quraysh, they divided the Book of God into parts. Others said: He meant by that a group of Salih’s people who had taken turns to keep Salih and his family company. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: As We sent down upon those who divided, he said: Those who divided for good, and he recited the statement of God Almighty: And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform, he said: They divided for God’s sake until he reached the verse. Some of them said: They are a people who divided up the roads of Mecca during the days of the pilgrims’ arrival upon them. Its people had sent them to punish it, and they had instructed some of them to spread the word in the area to which they were heading to to whoever asked him about the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from those coming to them, that he should say: He is crazy, and to another: He is a poet, and to some of them: He is a magician. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God the Most High commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform his people who had rejected the Qur’an and divided it, that he was a warner to them of the wrath and punishment of God the Most High, that what happened to those who divided before them and them, and what happened to those who divided before them, would befall them. It is possible that what was meant by those who divided was the People of the Two Books: the Torah and the Gospel, because they divided the Book of God. The Jews acknowledged some of the Torah and denied some of it, and denied the Gospel and the Criterion, and the Christians acknowledged some of the Gospel and denied some of it and the Criterion. It is possible that what was meant by this was the polytheists of Quraysh, because they divided the Qur’an, and some of them called it poetry, some called it soothsaying, and some called it legends of the ancients. It is possible that what was meant by this was the two groups. It is possible that it refers to those who divided it against Salih from his people. If there is no indication in the revelation that it refers to one of the three groups without the others, nor in a report from the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor in the innate nature of reason, and the apparent meaning of the verse is likely to be what I have described, then it must be decided that everyone who divided up God’s book by denying some and believing some, and divided up to disobey God, and upon whom the immediate punishment of God has befallen in this world, God’s book in this world before the revelation of this verse, is included in that because they were a lesson for their kind from the people of disbelief in God, and a lesson for those who learn from them from them. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his statement, Those who divided the Qur’an into parts. Some of them said: Its meaning is: Those who divided the Qur’an into separate sects. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Those who have divided the Qur’an into parts, he said: parts. Krayb and Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told us: Hisham told us: Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They divided him into parts, and they believed in some of him and disbelieved in some of him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: They cut it up and made it into parts like the parts of a camel. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Talha told us, on the authority of Ata’: Those who divided the Qur’an into parts, he said: The polytheists of Quraysh, they divided the Qur’an into parts, so some of them said: A magician, some of them said: A poet, and some of them said: A madman, and that is the part. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, They have divided the Qur’an into parts, that they have divided their book into parts like the parts of a camel, and that is because they cut it into sections, each party rejoicing in what they have, and that is His statement, They have divided their religion and become sects. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Those who have divided the Qur’an into parts, they have divided the Book of God. Some of them claimed that it was magic, some of them claimed that it was poetry, and some of them claimed that it was a soothsayer. Abu Jaafar said: This is what a soothsayer said, but it is only soothsaying. Some of them claimed that it is the legends of the ancients. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Those who divided the Qur’an into parts. He said: They believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. Yusun told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told me, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Those who have divided the Qur’an into parts, he said: They have divided it into parts as a sheep is divided. Some of them said: Divination. Some of them said: It is magic. Some of them said: Poetry. Some of them said: Legends of the ancients He has written down... the verse, they have divided it into parts as a sheep is divided. So the proponents of this statement explained his statement parts to the fact that its singular is: organ, and that parts is its plural, and that it is taken from their saying I divided something into parts: if I separated it, as Ru’bah said: God's religion is not a solution It means in detail, and as the other said: And the Banu Awf tribe was attacked, but their enemy was satisfied, and their pride was jealous. He means by his saying: And bit: he cursed them and cut them with his tongues. Others said: Rather, it is the plural of ‘udhah, the plural of ‘udhayn, just as barrah is pluralized as barin, and ‘uzah is ‘izzayn. So if this is directed to this interpretation, the original word is ‘udhah, and its original ha’ is gone, just as they removed the ha’ from ‘ash-shafa’, the original of which is ‘shafaha’, and from ‘ash-shata’, the original of which is ‘shaha’. This indicates that this is the original of their diminutive of ‘ash-shafa’: ‘shafiha’, and ‘ash-shata’: ‘shuwayha’, so they return the ha’ that is dropped in other than the case of the diminutive to it in the case of their diminutive. It is said from this: ‘I bit the man, I bit him, I bit him’: if I slandered him, and accused him of slander. And it is as if the interpretation of the one who interpreted this in this way is: those who bit the Qur’an, and they said: It is magic, or it is poetry, similar to the statement that we mentioned from Qatadah. A group of interpreters said: What he meant by the bite in this place is their attribution of it to magic in particular, without any other meanings of blame, as the poet said: The water from their bites is Zamzama Meaning: from their magic. Who said that? Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah: Those who have divided the Qur’an into parts. He said: Magic. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Adhin he said: They bit him and slandered him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Ikrimah used to say: Al-Adhah means magic in the language of Quraysh. You would say to a witch: She is the biter. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They have divided the Qur’an into parts, he said: magic, the parts of all the books, and the Quraysh, they divided the Qur’an, they said: it is magic. The correct thing to say about this is that God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform a people who had rejected the Qur’an that it was a warning to them of a punishment that would befall them, some of them like what was brought down on those who divided it. Their rejection of it was that they falsely accused it, and said that it was poetry and magic, and the like. We said that this is the most appropriate interpretation for it because what preceded it from the beginning of the surah and what followed it, which is His statement Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers, confirms the correctness of what we said, and that what he meant by His statement those who have divided the Qur’an into parts were the polytheists of his people. Since that is the case, it is known that there were no polytheists among his people who believed in some of the Qur’an and disbelieved in some of it, rather his people were in one of two meanings regarding his matter: either believing in all of it, or disbelieving in all of it. Since that is the case, the correct statement regarding the meaning of His statement those who have divided the Qur’an into parts is the statement of those who claimed that they had divided it. Some of them said: It is magic. Some of them said: It is poetry. Some of them said: It is divination, and similar statements, or they divided it and separated it, and similar statements. If that is what he meant, then his saying two parts could be the plural of bite, and it could be the plural of member, because the meaning of bite is to separate, just as camels and sheep are bitten, so their parts are separated. And bite is slander and false accusation of speech, so they are close in meaning.
15:92: God Almighty says: By your Lord, We will surely question them all.
15:93: God Almighty says: For what they used to do.
15:94: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: By your Lord, O Muhammad, we will surely ask those who made the Qur’an into a part in this world in the Hereafter about what they did in this world, in what We commanded them to do, and in what We sent you with to them from the verses of My Book that I revealed to them, and in what We called them to of acknowledging it, and of My Oneness and disavowing rivals and idols. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Abu Kuraib and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us: I heard Layth, on the authority of Bashir, on the authority of Anas, regarding his statement: By your Lord, We will surely question them all, he said: About the testimony that there is no god but God. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Bashir bin Nahik, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: By your Lord, we will surely question them all. He said: About there is no god but God. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Bashir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: By your Lord, We will surely question them all * About what they used to do, he said: About there is no god but God. Ahmad told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Hilal, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ukaim, who said: Abdullah said: By Him besides Whom there is no god, there is not one of you but that God will be alone with him on the Day of Resurrection, just as one of you is alone with the moon on the night of the full moon, and He will say: Son of Adam! What has deceived you about Me, O son of Adam? What did you do with what I did, O son of Adam? What did you answer the messengers? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, By your Lord, We will surely question them all * About what they used to do. He said: All the servants will be asked about two things on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:about what they used to worship, and about what they answered the messengers. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Al-Husayn Al-Ja’fi told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Umar, We will surely question them all * about what they used to do. He said: About there is no god but God. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, By your Lord, We will surely question them all * About what they used to do, then he said, On that Day no human being or jinn will be asked about his sin, he said: He will not ask them: Did you do such and such, because He knows that better than they do, but He will say to them: Why did you do such and such. Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God Almighty revealed, So proclaim what you are commanded, for it is a command from God Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to convey His message to his people and to all those to whom he was sent. What he meant by His statement, So proclaim what you are commanded, is: go forth and disperse, as Abu Dhu’ayb said: As if they were a lute, and as if it were joy overflowing onto the cup and cracking He means by his saying: to split: to separate with arrows. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then proclaim what you are commanded, meaning: then carry it out. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, So proclaim what you are commanded, meaning: Do what you are commanded. Al-Husayn bin Yazid Al-Tahan told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So proclaim what you are commanded, he said: the Qur’an. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me: Yahya bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: So proclaim what you are commanded. He said: It is the Qur’an. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So proclaim what you are commanded, he said: the Qur’an. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So proclaim what you are commanded, he said: Reciting the Qur’an aloud in prayer. Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: So proclaim what you are commanded, he said: with the Qur’an in prayer. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So proclaim what you are commanded, he said: Recite the Qur’an aloud in prayer. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Usama told us, he said: Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of his brother Abdullah bin Ubaidah, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to hide until the verse So proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists was revealed, so he and his companions went out. Yunus told me, he said: Abu Hab told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, So proclaim what you are commanded, he said: with the Qur’an that was revealed to him to convey to them. And God Almighty said, So proclaim what you are commanded, and He did not say: with what you are commanded with. And the command requires the preposition with, because the meaning of the statement is: So proclaim Our command, for We have commanded you to call to what We sent you with of the religion of creation, and We have given you permission to make it manifest. The meaning of ma in his statement by what you are commanded is the meaning of the source, as God Almighty said: O my father, do what you are commanded meaning: do the thing that you are commanded to do. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say about that: the ba that connects tu’mur was deleted from his statement fasda’ bima tu’mur in the language of those who say: I commanded you with something. And he used to say that the Arabs have two languages in that: one of them is I commanded you with something and the other is I commanded you with something. So he used to say: adding the ba in that and dropping it is the same, and he cited as evidence for his saying that the statement of Husayn ibn al-Mundhir al-Raqashi to Yazid ibn al-Muhallab: I gave you a firm order, but you disobeyed me, so you became deprived of your leadership and regretful. He said: I commanded you to do something, and he did not say: I commanded you to do something, and that is like what God Almighty said Indeed, the ‘Aad disbelieved in their Lord, and he did not say: in their Lord, and like what they said: I stretched the reins, and I stretched the reins, and similar words. As for His statement: And turn away from the polytheists, the Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Convey to your people what you were sent with, and refrain from waging war against the polytheists with God and fighting them, and that was before jihad against them was imposed upon him, then that was abrogated by His statement: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. As Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying and turn away from the polytheists is one of the abrogated verses. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwaid told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, regarding his statement, And turn away from the polytheists and Say to those who believe to forgive those who do not expect the days of God, and all of this is in the Qur’an. God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to do that from him, then He commanded fighting, so He abrogated all of that, and said, So seize them and kill them... the verse.
15:95: God Almighty says: Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers.
15:96: God Almighty says about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: We have sufficed you against the mockers, O Muhammad, who mock you and ridicule you. So proclaim God’s command and do not fear anything except God, for God will suffice you against your forelock and your harm, just as He sufficed you against the mockers. The leaders of the mockers were well-known people from Quraysh. Mention their names: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad told me: The great ones who mocked, as Yazid ibn Ruman told me, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, were five men from his people, and they were of advanced age and had honor among their people from Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza ibn Qusayy: al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib Abu Zama’ah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had, as far as I have been informed, prayed against him when he heard of his harm and mockery, saying: O God, blind his sight and bereave his children. From Banu Zuhra: al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth ibn Wahb ibn Abd Manaf ibn Zuhra. From Banu Makhzum: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah ibn Abdullah ibn Makhzum. From Banu Sahm ibn Amr ibn Hisais ibn Ka’b ibn Lu’ay: al-’As ibn Wa’il ibn Hisham ibn Sa’id ibn Sa’d ibn Sahm. From Khuza’ah: al-Harith ibn al-Talalatah ibn Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Amr ibn Malkan. When they persisted in their evil and increased their mockery of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God the Most High revealed: “So proclaim openly what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists. Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers”… until His saying: Then they will come to know. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ruman told me, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr or another scholar, that Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while they were circumambulating the House. He stood up, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood beside him. Al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib passed by him, and he threw a green leaf in his face, and he went blind. Al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth passed by him, and he pointed to his stomach, and his stomach ached, and he died of love. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira passed by him, and he pointed to the mark of a wound at the bottom of his heel that he had sustained two years before that, while he was dragging his garment, meaning his lower garment. That was because he passed by a man from Khuza’ah who was feathering his arrows, and one of his arrows got stuck in his lower garment, and scratched his leg. The scratch was nothing, so he pounced on it and killed him. Al-Aas bin Wael Al-Sahmi passed by him, so he pointed to the sole of his foot, so he went out on his donkey heading to Taif, and he came across Shabraqa, so a thorn entered the sole of his foot from it, and it killed him. Abu Jaafar said: Shabraqa is known as Hasak, from it comes Haban, and Haban is yellow water. Al-Harith Ibn Al-Talalatah passed by him, so he pointed to his head, and he blew pus, killing him. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad al-Qurashi, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Their leader was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and he was the one who gathered them. Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ziyad, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding His statement, Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers, he said: The mockers were: Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, Al-`As ibn Wa’il, Abu Zama’a, Al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth, and Al-Harith ibn `Aytala. Gabriel came to him and pointed with his finger to the head of Al-Walid and said: You did not do anything. He said: You are sufficient, and he pointed to the sole of Al-`As. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You did not do anything. He said: You are sufficient, and he pointed with his hand to the eye of Abu Zama’a. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You did not do anything. He said: You are sufficient, and he pointed with his finger to the head of Al-`As. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave my maternal uncle for me. He said: I am sufficient, and he pointed with his finger to the stomach of Al-Harith. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You did not do anything. He said: I am sufficient. He said: Al-Walid passed by a black mule of Khuza'ah while he was dragging his clothes, and a spark or a thorn got stuck to his clothes, and there were women in front of him, so he felt ashamed to step on anyone who would pull it off, and it started hitting his leg and scratched him, and he remained ill until he died. Al-'As bin Wa'il rode his white mule to do some errands at the bottom of Mecca, so he went to dismount and put the sole of his foot on a thorn, and it scratched his leg, and he continued scratching it until he died. Abu Zama'ah went blind, and the itch took hold of al-Aswad's head, and al-Harith took water into his stomach. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement, Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers, he said: They are five men from Quraysh 106:Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, Al-`As ibn Wa’il, Abu Zama`ah, Al-Harith ibn `Aytala, and Al-Aswad ibn Qays. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bashir, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers, he said: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, Al-Aas bin Zael Al-Sahmi, Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth, Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib, and Al-Harith bin Aitala. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers, he said: They are five, all of whom perished before Badr: Al-Aas bin Wa’il, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, Abu Zama’ah bin Abd Al-Aswad, Al-Harith bin Qais, and Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers. He said: Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, Al-Aas ibn Wa’il, Al-Aswad, and Al-Harith ibn Aitala. Al-Muthanna told us: Amr bin Awn told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, who said: I said to al-Zuhri: Sa`id bin Jubayr and `Ikrimah differed about a man among the mockers. Sa`id said: He is al-Harith bin `Aytala, and `Ikrimah said: He is al-Harith bin Qays. He said: They spoke the truth. There was a slave woman called `Aytala, and his father was Qays. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: The mockers are seven, and he named four of them. Ibn Wakee’ told us, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Aamer: Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers. He said: There were five men from Quraysh 106:Al-Aas ibn Wa’il Al-Sahmi, who was sufficed with a headache that affected his head, and his brain was flowing until he was speaking through his nose; Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah Al-Makhzumi, who was sufficed by a man from Khuza’ah who had fixed an arrow of his, and a splinter of it came off, and he stepped on it and died; Hubbar ibn Al-Aswad, Abd Yaghuth ibn Wahb, and Al-Harith ibn ‘Aytala. Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Aamer: Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers. He said: All of them were from Quraysh 106:Al-Aas ibn Wa’il, who was sufficed by a headache that caused his brain to flow so that he could not speak except from under his nose; Al-Harith ibn ‘Aytala, who had a yellow spot in his stomach; Ibn al-Aswad, who was sufficed by smallpox; Al-Walid, who had a man go to fix an arrow of his, and a splinter fell and he stepped on it; and Abd Yaghuth, who was sufficed by blindness, he lost his sight. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Muqsim, Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers. He said: They are al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-'As ibn Wa'il, 'Adi ibn Qays, al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth, and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib. They passed by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, man by man, and Gabriel was with him. When one of them passed by, Gabriel would say: How do you find this man? He would say: What a bad enemy of God! Gabriel would say: Suffice him! As for al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, he fell down, and an arrow caught on his cloak. He went to sit down, but it cut his kohl, and he bled and died. As for al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth, a thorny branch was brought to him, and he struck him in the face with it, and his pupils flowed down his face. He would say: I made a supplication against Muhammad, and I made a supplication against me, and it was answered for me, and it was answered for him. I made a supplication against me that I should go blind, and I went blind. I made a supplication against him that he should be alone and unique among the people of Yathrib, and so it was. As for Al-Aas bin Wael, he stepped on a thorn and his flesh fell off his bones until he died. As for Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib and Adi bin Qais, one of them got up at night while he was thirsty and drank water from a jar. He kept drinking until he thought his mouth burst and he died. As for the other, a snake bit him and he died. Al-Hasan bin Yahya urged us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of Qatada and Uthman, on the authority of Muqsim, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers. Then he mentioned something similar to what Ibn Abd al-A’la narrated, on the authority of Ibn Thawr. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: As We sent down to the dividers * Who divided the Qur’an into parts. They were a group of five from Quraysh, who divided the Qur’an into parts. Some of them claimed that it was magic, some of them claimed that it was poetry, and some of them claimed that it was legends of the ancients. As for one of them: Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth, he came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was at the House, and he said to him: How do you find this? He said: What a bad servant of God, even though he is my uncle. He said: We have sufficed you. Then Adi bin Qais, the brother of Banu Sahm, came to him, and the king said: How do you find this? He said: What a bad servant of God. He said: We have sufficed you. Then Al-Aswad Abdul Muttalib came to him, and the king said to him: How do you find this? He said: What a bad servant of God. He said: We have sufficed you. Then Al-Aas bin Wa’il came to him, and the king said to him: How do you find this? He said: What a bad servant of God. He said: We have sufficed you. As for Al-Aswad bin Yaghuth, a thorny branch was brought to him and he struck his face with it until his pupils flowed down his face. After that, he used to say: Muhammad made a supplication against me, and I made another supplication against him, so God answered him in me, and God answered me in him. He supplicated that I should be bereaved and blinded, and that was the case. I supplicated that he should become a fugitive and an outcast, so we expelled him with the Jews of Yathrib and the thieves of the pilgrims, and that was the case. As for Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, he went to put on his cloak, but an arrow caught his cloak and hit his cloak or his head, and he was struck in both cases and died. As for Al-Aas bin Wa’il, he stepped on a thorn, and that was the case, and his flesh began to fall off limb by limb, and he died in that state. As for Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib and Adi bin Qais, I do not know what happened to them. “It was mentioned to us that on the day of Badr, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade his companions from killing Abu al-Bakhtari, and said: Take him, for he has been a scourge. The companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: O Abu al-Bakhtari, we have been forbidden from killing you, so come to safety and security. Abu al-Bakhtari said: And my nephew is with me. They said: We were not commanded except for you. They tried to tempt him three times, but he refused except with his nephew with him. He said: So he spoke harshly to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a man from the people attacked him and stabbed him and killed him. Then his killer came as if a mountain had been on his back, tying him down, for fear that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would blame him. When he was informed of what he had said, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God distance him and crush him.” They are the mockers about whom God said: Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers. They are the five to whom it was said: Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers. They mocked the Book of God and His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers - they are from Quraysh. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Ibn Abi Bazza claimed that they were Al-Aas bin Wa’il Al-Sahmi, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah Al-Wahid, Al-Harith bin Adi bin Sahm bin Al-Aytalah, Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib bin Asad bin Abdul-Uzza bin Qusayy, who is Abu Zama’ah, and Al-Aswad bin Abdul-Yaghuth, who is the maternal cousin of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qasim told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Amr ibn Dinar told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similar to the hadith of Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Thawr, except that he said: There were eight of them, then he counted them and said: All of them died before Badr. His saying, Those who make another god with God - they will soon know. This is a warning from God Almighty, and a threat to the mockers, whom His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed that He had sufficed him with their matter by saying, Almighty and Exalted be He: “Indeed, We have sufficed you, O Muhammad, against those who mock you, who make a partner with God in His worship. They will soon know what they will encounter of God’s punishment when they return to Him on the Day of Resurrection, and what calamity will befall them.”
15:97: God Almighty says: And We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say.
15:98: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And indeed, we know, O Muhammad, that your chest is constricted by what these polytheists among your people say of their denial of you and their mockery of you and what you have brought to them, and that this embarrasses you. So glorify the praises of your Lord. He says: So resort to thanking God and praising Him and praying in response to what has befallen you that you dislike from them. God will suffice you from that which concerns you. This is similar to the report that was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that if something distressed him, he would resort to prayer.
15:99: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And worship your Lord until death comes to you, of which you are certain. It was said: certainty, and he is certain, just as it was said: old wine, and it is aged. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: Tariq bin Abdul Rahman told me, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty. He said: Death. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, all of them on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Abbas bin Muhammad told me, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Kathir told me that he heard Mujahid say: Until the certainty comes to you, he said: death. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you, he said: He means death. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Until the certainty comes to you. He said: The certainty is death. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Mubarak bin Fadala, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement: Until the certainty comes to you, he said: Death. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Tariq, on the authority of Salim, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty, he said: Death, when death comes to him, the confirmation of what God said to him comes to him, and He tells him about the matter of the Hereafter. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yunus bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, “that Kharijah bin Zaid bin Thabit told him on the authority of Umm al-Ala, a woman of the Ansar, who had pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She told him that they had divided the Muhajireen by lot. She said: ‘Uthman bin Maz’un flew to us, so we put him up in our houses, and he suffered the illness in which he died. When he died and was washed and shrouded in his clothes, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered, and I said: O Uthman bin Maz’un, may God have mercy on you, Abu al-Sa’ib, for my testimony is upon you, God has honored you.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘As for him, certainty has come to him, and by God, I hope good for him.’” Abu Kuraib told us: Malik bin Ismail told us: Ismail told us: Ibrahim bin Saad told us: Ibn Shihab told us, on the authority of Kharijah bin Zaid, on the authority of Umm al-Ala, one of their women, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Jaafar bin Awn told us: Ibrahim bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Shihab, that Kharijah bin Zaid told him, on the authority of Umm Al-Ala, a woman from among them, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar, except that he said in his hadith: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for him, he has witnessed certainty.
